tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

action.description:
The action to perform:

* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

"""AI system prompts in the "Angebote" administration (tab "Prompts")."""

import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator, Awaitable, Callable
from typing import Any

import reflex as rx

from alloq_offer.admin.states.offer_admin_state import admin_name
from alloq_offer.workshop.services import prompts as prompt_store
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.prompts import PromptError
from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session
from appkit_user.authentication.decorators import requires_admin

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

LOAD_ERROR = "Die Prompts konnten nicht geladen werden."
SAVE_ERROR = "Der Prompt konnte nicht gespeichert werden."
SAVED = "Der Prompt wurde als neue Version gespeichert und ist aktiv."
ACTIVATED = "Diese Version des Prompts ist jetzt aktiv."


class PromptAdminState(rx.State):
    """Admins save new versions of the system prompts or go back to older ones."""

    prompts: rx.Field[list[dict[str, Any]]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    name: rx.Field[str] = rx.field(prompt_store.CHAPTER_PROMPT)
    text: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    versions: rx.Field[list[dict[str, Any]]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)

    @rx.var
    def selected(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return next((p for p in self.prompts if p["name"] == self.name), {})

    @rx.var
    def changed(self) -> bool:
        return self.text.strip() != str(self.selected.get("text", "")).strip()

    async def _reload(self) -> None:
        self.prompts = await prompt_store.list_prompts(get_asyncdb_session)
        self.text = str(self.selected.get("text", ""))
        self.versions = await prompt_store.prompt_versions(
            get_asyncdb_session, self.name
        )

    async def _guarded(
        self, error: str, action: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]] | None = None
    ) -> Any:
        """Run ``action`` (if any) and reload; a toast when it failed."""
        try:
            if action is not None:
                await action()
            await self._reload()
        except PromptError as exc:
            return rx.toast.error(str(exc), position="top-right")
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Prompt %s: %s", self.name, error)
            return rx.toast.error(error, position="top-right")
        return None

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def load_prompts(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        yield await self._guarded(LOAD_ERROR)

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def select_prompt(self, name: str) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        if name not in prompt_store.PROMPT_NAMES:
            return
        self.name = name
        yield await self._guarded(LOAD_ERROR)

    @rx.event
    def set_text(self, value: str) -> None:
        self.text = value

    @requires_admin

"""Template drafts in admin: outline, Word layout and publishing (spec 6.1).

The draft outline points at library blocks. Publishing copies the outline with
every block setting and the layout into a new immutable version; offers that
bound an older version are not touched.
"""

import io
import logging
import zipfile
from typing import Any

from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import BlobEntity
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import (
    SETTINGS_FIELDS,
    TemplateError,
    TemplatePackage,
    clean_layout,
    frame_headings,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.exports import DOCX_MIME
from alloq_offer.workshop.storage import BlobStore, BlobTooLargeError
from alloq_offer.workshop.template_entities import (
    ChapterBlockEntity,
    OfferTemplateChapterEntity,
    OfferTemplateEntity,
    OfferTemplateVersionEntity,
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_TITLE = 255
# A layout unpacks to at most this much, so a crafted zip cannot exhaust memory.
MAX_UNPACKED_BYTES = 200 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_PARTS = 2000
NOT_FOUND = "Diese Vorlage gibt es nicht."
NO_ENTRY = "Diesen Eintrag der Gliederung gibt es nicht."
NO_BLOCK = "Diesen aktiven Kapitelbaustein gibt es nicht."
BLOCK_IN_OUTLINE = "Der Baustein ist schon in der Gliederung."
NOT_DOCX = "Bitte laden Sie eine Word-Datei (.docx) hoch."
TOO_LARGE = "Die Datei ist zu groß."
NO_LAYOUT = "Bitte laden Sie zuerst ein Word-Layout hoch."
EMPTY_OUTLINE = "Die Gliederung braucht mindestens ein Kapitel."
TITLE_TOO_LONG = "Die Überschrift darf höchstens 255 Zeichen haben."
BAD_LEVEL = "Ein Kapitel hat die Ebene 1 oder 2."
INVALID_DRAFT = "Die Vorlage ist so nicht gültig. Bitte prüfen Sie die Bausteine."


class DraftError(ValueError):
    """The draft cannot be changed or published; the message is German."""


async def list_templates(sessions: SessionFactory) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.execute(
                select(
                    OfferTemplateEntity,
                    func.max(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.number),
                )
                .outerjoin(OfferTemplateVersionEntity)
                .group_by(OfferTemplateEntity.id)
                .order_by(OfferTemplateEntity.name)
            )
        ).all()
    return [{**template.to_dict(), "latest": latest or 0} for template, latest in rows]


async def _template(session: AsyncSession, template_id: int) -> OfferTemplateEntity:
    template = await session.get(OfferTemplateEntity, template_id, with_for_update=True)
    if template is None:
        raise DraftError(NOT_FOUND)
    return template


async def _entries(
    session: AsyncSession, template_id: int
) -> list[tuple[OfferTemplateChapterEntity, ChapterBlockEntity]]:
    rows = await session.execute(
        select(OfferTemplateChapterEntity, ChapterBlockEntity)
        .join(ChapterBlockEntity)
        .where(OfferTemplateChapterEntity.template_id == template_id)
        .order_by(OfferTemplateChapterEntity.position, OfferTemplateChapterEntity.id)
    )
    return [(entry, block) for entry, block in rows.all()]


def _renumber(entries: list[OfferTemplateChapterEntity]) -> None:
    for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
        entry.position = position


async def load_outline(
    sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """The draft outline with the title and level each entry will publish."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        entries = await _entries(session, template_id)
    return [
        {
            "id": entry.id,
            "block_key": block.key,
            "block_title": block.title,
            "type": block.chapter_type,
            "title": entry.title or block.title,
            "title_override": entry.title or "",
            "level": entry.level or block.level,
            "level_override": entry.level or 0,
            "required": entry.required,
            "active": block.active,
        }
        for entry, block in entries
    ]


class TemplateDraft:
    """Changes to the draft of one template; each locks the template row."""

    def __init__(self, sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int) -> None:
        self._sessions = sessions
        self._template_id = template_id

    async def _entry(
        self, session: AsyncSession, entry_id: int
    ) -> OfferTemplateChapterEntity:
        await _template(session, self._template_id)
        entry = await session.get(OfferTemplateChapterEntity, entry_id)
        if entry is None or entry.template_id != self._template_id:
            raise DraftError(NO_ENTRY)
        return entry

    async def add_block(self, block_key: str) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            await _template(session, self._template_id)
            block = await session.scalar(
                select(ChapterBlockEntity).where(
                    ChapterBlockEntity.key == block_key, ChapterBlockEntity.active
                )
            )
            if block is None:
                raise DraftError(NO_BLOCK)
            entries = [entry for entry, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)]
            if any(entry.block_id == block.id for entry in entries):
                raise DraftError(BLOCK_IN_OUTLINE)
            session.add(
                OfferTemplateChapterEntity(
                    template_id=self._template_id,
                    block_id=block.id,
                    position=len(entries),
                    required=False,
                )
            )

    async def remove(self, entry_id: int) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            await session.delete(entry)
            await session.flush()
            _renumber([e for e, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)])

    async def move(self, entry_id: int, index: int) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            entries = [
                e
                for e, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)
                if e.id != entry.id
            ]
            entries.insert(max(0, min(index, len(entries))), entry)
            _renumber(entries)

    async def update(
        self, entry_id: int, *, required: bool, title: str, level: int | None
    ) -> None:
        """Required flag and the title and level that override the block's."""
        name = title.strip()
        if len(name) > MAX_TITLE:
            raise DraftError(TITLE_TOO_LONG)
        if level not in (None, 1, 2):
            raise DraftError(BAD_LEVEL)
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            entry.required = required
            entry.title = name or None
            entry.level = level

    async def upload_layout(self, store: BlobStore, filename: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        """Check, clean and keep a Word layout; its frame headings are read off it."""
        if not filename.lower().endswith(".docx"):
            raise DraftError(NOT_DOCX)
        _check_zip(data)
        try:
            cleaned = clean_layout(data)
            before, after = frame_headings(cleaned)
        except TemplateError as exc:
            raise DraftError(str(exc)) from exc
        try:
            blob_id = await store.put(cleaned, DOCX_MIME)
        except BlobTooLargeError as exc:
            raise DraftError(TOO_LARGE) from exc
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            template = await _template(session, self._template_id)
            template.draft_layout_blob_id = blob_id
            template.frame_before = before
            template.frame_after = after
        logger.info("Layout of template %s replaced", self._template_id)

    async def publish(self, user: str) -> int:
        """Store the draft as the next immutable version; returns its number."""
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            template = await _template(session, self._template_id)
            if template.draft_layout_blob_id is None:
                raise DraftError(NO_LAYOUT)
            entries = await _entries(session, self._template_id)
            if not entries:
                raise DraftError(EMPTY_OUTLINE)
            layout = await session.scalar(
                select(BlobEntity.data).where(
                    BlobEntity.id == template.draft_layout_blob_id
                )
            )
            payload = {
                "chapters": [_resolved(entry, block) for entry, block in entries],
                "frame_before": list(template.frame_before),
                "frame_after": list(template.frame_after),
            }
            try:
                TemplatePackage.model_validate(
                    {
                        **payload,
                        "key": template.key,
                        "version": "0",
                        "layout_bytes": layout,
                    }
                )
            except (ValidationError, TemplateError) as exc:
                logger.warning("Template %s does not validate: %s", template.key, exc)
                raise DraftError(INVALID_DRAFT) from exc
            number = (
                await session.scalar(
                    select(func.max(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.number)).where(
                        OfferTemplateVersionEntity.template_id == template.id
                    )
                )
                or 0
            ) + 1
            session.add(
                OfferTemplateVersionEntity(
                    template_id=template.id,
                    number=number,
                    payload=payload,
                    layout_blob_id=template.draft_layout_blob_id,
                    published_by=user,
                )
            )
        logger.info("Template %s published as version %s", self._template_id, number)
        return number


def _resolved(
    entry: OfferTemplateChapterEntity, block: ChapterBlockEntity
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "key": block.key,
        "title": entry.title or block.title,
        "level": entry.level or block.level,
        "required": entry.required,
        "chapter_type": block.chapter_type,
        "default_content": block.default_content,
        **{name: getattr(block, name) for name in SETTINGS_FIELDS},
    }


def _check_zip(data: bytes) -> None:
    """Refuse files that are no zip or would unpack to too much."""
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
            parts = archive.infolist()
    except zipfile.BadZipFile as exc:
        raise DraftError(NOT_DOCX) from exc
    if len(parts) > MAX_PARTS or sum(p.file_size for p in parts) > MAX_UNPACKED_BYTES:
        raise DraftError(TOO_LARGE)


async def list_versions(
    sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Published versions, newest first."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(
                select(OfferTemplateVersionEntity)
                .where(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.template_id == template_id)
                .order_by(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.number.desc())
            )
        ).all()
    return [
        {
            "number": row.number,
            "published_by": row.published_by,
            "created": row.created.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"),
            "chapters": len(row.payload.get("chapters", [])),
        }
        for row in rows
    ]

) -> list[tuple[OfferTemplateChapterEntity, ChapterBlockEntity]]:
    rows = await session.execute(
        select(OfferTemplateChapterEntity, ChapterBlockEntity)
        .join(ChapterBlockEntity)
        .where(OfferTemplateChapterEntity.template_id == template_id)
        .order_by(OfferTemplateChapterEntity.position, OfferTemplateChapterEntity.id)
    )
    return [(entry, block) for entry, block in rows.all()]


def _renumber(entries: list[OfferTemplateChapterEntity]) -> None:
    for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
        entry.position = position


async def load_outline(
    sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """The draft outline with the title and level each entry will publish."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        entries = await _entries(session, template_id)
    return [
        {
            "id": entry.id,
            "block_key": block.key,
            "block_title": block.title,
            "type": block.chapter_type,
            "title": entry.title or block.title,
            "title_override": entry.title or "",
            "level": entry.level or block.level,
            "level_override": entry.level or 0,
            "required": entry.required,
            "active": block.active,
        }
        for entry, block in entries
    ]


class TemplateDraft:
    """Changes to the draft of one template; each locks the template row."""

    def __init__(self, sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int) -> None:
        self._sessions = sessions
        self._template_id = template_id

    async def _entry(
        self, session: AsyncSession, entry_id: int
    ) -> OfferTemplateChapterEntity:
        await _template(session, self._template_id)
        entry = await session.get(OfferTemplateChapterEntity, entry_id)
        if entry is None or entry.template_id != self._template_id:
            raise DraftError(NO_ENTRY)
        return entry

    async def add_block(self, block_key: str) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            await _template(session, self._template_id)
            block = await session.scalar(
                select(ChapterBlockEntity).where(
                    ChapterBlockEntity.key == block_key, ChapterBlockEntity.active
                )
            )
            if block is None:
                raise DraftError(NO_BLOCK)
            entries = [entry for entry, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)]
            if any(entry.block_id == block.id for entry in entries):
                raise DraftError(BLOCK_IN_OUTLINE)
            session.add(
                OfferTemplateChapterEntity(
                    template_id=self._template_id,
                    block_id=block.id,
                    position=len(entries),
                    required=False,
                )
            )

    async def remove(self, entry_id: int) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            await session.delete(entry)
            await session.flush()
            _renumber([e for e, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)])

    async def move(self, entry_id: int, index: int) -> None:
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            entries = [
                e
                for e, _ in await _entries(session, self._template_id)
                if e.id != entry.id
            ]
            entries.insert(max(0, min(index, len(entries))), entry)
            _renumber(entries)

    async def update(
        self, entry_id: int, *, required: bool, title: str, level: int | None
    ) -> None:
        """Required flag and the title and level that override the block's."""
        name = title.strip()
        if len(name) > MAX_TITLE:
            raise DraftError(TITLE_TOO_LONG)
        if level not in (None, 1, 2):
            raise DraftError(BAD_LEVEL)
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            entry = await self._entry(session, entry_id)
            entry.required = required
            entry.title = name or None
            entry.level = level

    async def upload_layout(self, store: BlobStore, filename: str, data: bytes) -> None:
        """Check, clean and keep a Word layout; its frame headings are read off it."""
        if not filename.lower().endswith(".docx"):
            raise DraftError(NOT_DOCX)
        _check_zip(data)
        try:
            cleaned = clean_layout(data)
            before, after = frame_headings(cleaned)
        except TemplateError as exc:
            raise DraftError(str(exc)) from exc
        try:
            blob_id = await store.put(cleaned, DOCX_MIME)
        except BlobTooLargeError as exc:
            raise DraftError(TOO_LARGE) from exc
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            template = await _template(session, self._template_id)
            template.draft_layout_blob_id = blob_id
            template.frame_before = before
            template.frame_after = after
        logger.info("Layout of template %s replaced", self._template_id)

    async def publish(self, user: str) -> int:
        """Store the draft as the next immutable version; returns its number."""
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            template = await _template(session, self._template_id)
            if template.draft_layout_blob_id is None:
                raise DraftError(NO_LAYOUT)
            entries = await _entries(session, self._template_id)
            if not entries:
                raise DraftError(EMPTY_OUTLINE)
            layout = await session.scalar(
                select(BlobEntity.data).where(
                    BlobEntity.id == template.draft_layout_blob_id
                )
            )
            payload = {
                "chapters": [_resolved(entry, block) for entry, block in entries],
                "frame_before": list(template.frame_before),
                "frame_after": list(template.frame_after),
            }
            try:
                TemplatePackage.model_validate(
                    {
                        **payload,
                        "key": template.key,
                        "version": "0",
                        "layout_bytes": layout,
                    }
                )
            except (ValidationError, TemplateError) as exc:
                logger.warning("Template %s does not validate: %s", template.key, exc)
                raise DraftError(INVALID_DRAFT) from exc
            number = (
                await session.scalar(
                    select(func.max(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.number)).where(
                        OfferTemplateVersionEntity.template_id == template.id
                    )
                )
                or 0
            ) + 1
            session.add(
                OfferTemplateVersionEntity(
                    template_id=template.id,
                    number=number,
                    payload=payload,
                    layout_blob_id=template.draft_layout_blob_id,
                    published_by=user,
                )
            )
        logger.info("Template %s published as version %s", self._template_id, number)
        return number


def _resolved(
    entry: OfferTemplateChapterEntity, block: ChapterBlockEntity
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "key": block.key,
        "title": entry.title or block.title,
        "level": entry.level or block.level,
        "required": entry.required,
        "chapter_type": block.chapter_type,
        "default_content": block.default_content,
        **{name: getattr(block, name) for name in SETTINGS_FIELDS},
    }


def _check_zip(data: bytes) -> None:
    """Refuse files that are no zip or would unpack to too much."""
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(data)) as archive:
            parts = archive.infolist()
    except zipfile.BadZipFile as exc:
        raise DraftError(NOT_DOCX) from exc
    if len(parts) > MAX_PARTS or sum(p.file_size for p in parts) > MAX_UNPACKED_BYTES:
        raise DraftError(TOO_LARGE)


async def list_versions(
    sessions: SessionFactory, template_id: int
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Published versions, newest first."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(
                select(OfferTemplateVersionEntity)
                .where(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.template_id == template_id)
                .order_by(OfferTemplateVersionEntity.number.desc())
            )
        ).all()
    return [
        {
            "number": row.number,
            "published_by": row.published_by,
            "created": row.created.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"),
            "chapters": len(row.payload.get("chapters", [])),
        }
        for row in rows
    ]

## Phase 6: Docs
Update `spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (sections 5.5 and 6.1) and the matching page under
`docs/features/` for the new outline rules, the admin menu and template versions. Run the
`docs-sync` agent at the end.

---

## Tests (write first, per phase)
- Migration: `migration-reviewer` agent; a test that the seed payload parses into
  `TemplatePackage` and every `default_content` passes `parse_content`.
- `services/templates.py`: load by version, cache, unknown version error, layout check.
- Outline service: add from block and blank, remove required refused, soft delete and
  restore, move keeps frame and positions dense, numbering function (1, 2, 2.1, 3), conflict
  and protection rules, `requires_offer_editor` in `test_workshop_authorization.py`.
- Export snapshot and docx: order by position, removed chapters skipped, added chapter
  exported with its title and level.
- Draft job and findings use per-chapter `settings` and the chapter's prompt text; prompt
  version recorded as `name@version`.
- States: outline mixin handlers (select, reorder, add dialog, remove confirm), admin states
  (create block, publish template, upload invalid layout, prompt version activate), each
  refusing non-admins.
- Update existing tests that depend on YAML files (`test_workshop_template.py`,
  `test_workshop_chapters.py`, `test_workshop_chapter_state.py`, others found by grep for
  `load_template` and `chapters.yaml`).
- Coverage ≥ 80% for the new services and states.

## Success criteria
- `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` pass; no file over 1000 lines.
- Local visual check (chrome-devtools isolated context, local test login): the Kapitel tab
  matches the prototype layout; only the selected chapter shows its floating toolbar
  hovering over the block's top edge, and it stays visible while scrolling a long chapter;
  dragging a chapter
  in the outline reorders document and numbering and survives a reload; required chapters
  have no "Entfernen"; frame entries cannot be dragged; "+ Kapitel" adds a library block with
  its default content and a blank chapter.
- In `/admin/offers` an admin creates a block, adds it to a template, uploads a layout,
  publishes version 2; a new offer uses version 2, an existing offer still shows version 1.
- Editing the chapter prompt in admin changes the next AI chapter draft; the generation run
  shows the new prompt version.
- Word export of an offer with a moved and an added chapter has the right order, numbering
  and frame.
- The user runs the Alembic upgrade; Claude only hands over the command.

## Out of scope
- Story scope selection (the prototype's "Enthält Stories mit Scope" checkboxes). Scope was
  removed on purpose in the last commit; the stories panel only offers grouping.
- Moving the Branchen page into the new menu.
- Live multi-user editing in one chapter; the one-editor-per-chapter rule and conflict
  check stay.
- Migrating existing offers to a newer template version.
- New chapter types beyond prose, table, stories and calc.

  2. `workshop/services/template_drafts.py:213-262` (`publish`) and `template_admin_state.py:181-195`.

     - The `FOR UPDATE` on the template row serializes the version numbers, so there is no integrity problem. But versions are immutable, so the duplicates stay.

Mit offenen Punkten darf weitergearbeitet werden. Der Umgang mit kritischen Scope-Konflikten und kommerziellen Festlegungen bleibt ausdrücklich geregelt. Eine vollständige Einzelbestätigung aller extrahierten Sätze oder jedes Bearbeitungsschritts ist nicht erforderlich.

### 5.5 Kapitel erstellen und bearbeiten

Erst auf Basis einer versionierten Map werden die Kapitel der Vorlage entworfen. Nutzer können Texte und Tabellen bearbeiten, Abschnitte ergänzen und gezielt KI-Vorschläge anfordern. Die zugehörigen Stories bleiben erreichbar. Map und Story-Katalog sind gespeicherte Fachobjekte; ihre Darstellung im Kapiteltext ist eine Projektion desselben Stands.

Neue Vorschläge erscheinen als Vergleich zum aktuellen Stand. Erst die Übernahme ändert den verbindlichen Inhalt. Ein leeres Unternehmenswissensarchiv verhindert weder Map noch Stories oder Kapitelentwurf.

### 5.6 Word erzeugen

Vor dem Export werden alle Änderungen gespeichert und ein fester Dokumentstand gebildet. Der Nutzer sieht die Ausgabeart und vorhandene Blocker. Der Export verwendet diesen Stand sowie die zugeordnete Version der Word-Vorlage. Spätere Bearbeitungen verändern eine bereits erzeugte Datei nicht.

## 6. Vorlagenmodell: vorhandenes Word und bearbeitbare Kapitel

### 6.1 Ein versioniertes Vorlagenpaket

Ein Vorlagenpaket besteht aus drei zusammengehörigen Teilen:

| Bestandteil | Aufgabe |
|---|---|
| Kapiteldefinition | Stabile Kapitel-IDs, Pflichtstatus und Inhaltsregeln; die User Story Map beginnt den fachlichen Inhalt, gefolgt von verknüpften Stories und Angebotskapiteln |
| Word-Layoutdatei | Bestehende Corporate-Vorlage mit Formatvorlagen, Kopf- und Fußzeilen, Platzhaltern und wiederholbaren Bereichen |
| Generierungs- und Prüfregeln | Leitfragen, Stil, verbindliche Textbausteine, benötigte Informationen und kapitelbezogene Prüfungen |

Alle Teile werden gemeinsam versioniert und auf Kompatibilität geprüft. Ein Angebot bindet eine konkrete Paketversion. Ein Vorlagenwechsel ist eine ausdrückliche Migration mit Vorschau; er verändert vorhandene Angebote nicht automatisch.

### 6.2 Übernahme der bestehenden Word-Vorlage

1. **Inventarisieren:** Kapitel, Formatvorlagen, Tabellen, Nummerierung, Inhaltsverzeichnis, Abschnitte, Bilder, Pflichtformulierungen und Formularfelder erfassen. Die User Story Map mit verknüpftem Story-Katalog am Beginn des fachlichen Inhalts verankern; fehlt dieser Bereich, wird die Vorlage gezielt ergänzt.
2. **Inhalt zuordnen:** Veränderliche Bereiche erhalten stabile IDs. Feste Texte und durch Nutzer editierbare Bereiche werden ausdrücklich ausgewiesen.
3. **Technisch vorbereiten:** Geeignete Platzhalter und Wiederholungsbereiche in einer Kopie der Vorlage ergänzen. Generierter Inhalt darf keine neue Vorlagenlogik ausführen.
4. **Fähigkeiten testen:** Eine Referenzdatei mit kurzen und langen Kapiteln, Tabellen, Listen und Sonderzeichen erzeugen. Mit der Ausgangsvorlage in Word vergleichen.
5. **Paket freigeben:** Nur geprüfte Kombinationen aus Layout, Kapiteldefinition und Exporter werden angeboten.

Ein automatischer Erstvorschlag für die Kapitelzuordnung ist möglich. Die beliebige, verlustfreie Umwandlung jeder Word-Datei in einen Webeditor wird nicht vorausgesetzt. Komplexe Textfelder, verschachtelte Tabellen, spezielle Nummerierung und eingebettete Objekte können eine Anpassung der Vorlage erfordern.

Mit offenen Punkten darf weitergearbeitet werden. Der Umgang mit kritischen Scope-Konflikten und kommerziellen Festlegungen bleibt ausdrücklich geregelt. Eine vollständige Einzelbestätigung aller extrahierten Sätze oder jedes Bearbeitungsschritts ist nicht erforderlich.

### 5.5 Kapitel erstellen und bearbeiten

Erst auf Basis einer versionierten Map werden die Kapitel der Vorlage entworfen. Nutzer können Texte und Tabellen bearbeiten, Abschnitte ergänzen und gezielt KI-Vorschläge anfordern. Die zugehörigen Stories bleiben erreichbar. Map und Story-Katalog sind gespeicherte Fachobjekte; ihre Darstellung im Kapiteltext ist eine Projektion desselben Stands.

Neue Vorschläge erscheinen als Vergleich zum aktuellen Stand. Erst die Übernahme ändert den verbindlichen Inhalt. Ein leeres Unternehmenswissensarchiv verhindert weder Map noch Stories oder Kapitelentwurf.

### 5.6 Word erzeugen

Vor dem Export werden alle Änderungen gespeichert und ein fester Dokumentstand gebildet. Der Nutzer sieht die Ausgabeart und vorhandene Blocker. Der Export verwendet diesen Stand sowie die zugeordnete Version der Word-Vorlage. Spätere Bearbeitungen verändern eine bereits erzeugte Datei nicht.

## 6. Vorlagenmodell: vorhandenes Word und bearbeitbare Kapitel

### 6.1 Ein versioniertes Vorlagenpaket

Ein Vorlagenpaket besteht aus drei zusammengehörigen Teilen:

| Bestandteil | Aufgabe |
|---|---|
| Kapiteldefinition | Stabile Kapitel-IDs, Pflichtstatus und Inhaltsregeln; die User Story Map beginnt den fachlichen Inhalt, gefolgt von verknüpften Stories und Angebotskapiteln |
| Word-Layoutdatei | Bestehende Corporate-Vorlage mit Formatvorlagen, Kopf- und Fußzeilen, Platzhaltern und wiederholbaren Bereichen |
| Generierungs- und Prüfregeln | Leitfragen, Stil, verbindliche Textbausteine, benötigte Informationen und kapitelbezogene Prüfungen |

Alle Teile werden gemeinsam versioniert und auf Kompatibilität geprüft. Ein Angebot bindet eine konkrete Paketversion. Ein Vorlagenwechsel ist eine ausdrückliche Migration mit Vorschau; er verändert vorhandene Angebote nicht automatisch.

### 6.2 Übernahme der bestehenden Word-Vorlage

1. **Inventarisieren:** Kapitel, Formatvorlagen, Tabellen, Nummerierung, Inhaltsverzeichnis, Abschnitte, Bilder, Pflichtformulierungen und Formularfelder erfassen. Die User Story Map mit verknüpftem Story-Katalog am Beginn des fachlichen Inhalts verankern; fehlt dieser Bereich, wird die Vorlage gezielt ergänzt.
2. **Inhalt zuordnen:** Veränderliche Bereiche erhalten stabile IDs. Feste Texte und durch Nutzer editierbare Bereiche werden ausdrücklich ausgewiesen.
3. **Technisch vorbereiten:** Geeignete Platzhalter und Wiederholungsbereiche in einer Kopie der Vorlage ergänzen. Generierter Inhalt darf keine neue Vorlagenlogik ausführen.
4. **Fähigkeiten testen:** Eine Referenzdatei mit kurzen und langen Kapiteln, Tabellen, Listen und Sonderzeichen erzeugen. Mit der Ausgangsvorlage in Word vergleichen.
5. **Paket freigeben:** Nur geprüfte Kombinationen aus Layout, Kapiteldefinition und Exporter werden angeboten.

Ein automatischer Erstvorschlag für die Kapitelzuordnung ist möglich. Die beliebige, verlustfreie Umwandlung jeder Word-Datei in einen Webeditor wird nicht vorausgesetzt. Komplexe Textfelder, verschachtelte Tabellen, spezielle Nummerierung und eingebettete Objekte können eine Anpassung der Vorlage erfordern.

def _start_content(form: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The start content of the block from the type specific fields."""
    kind = form["chapter_type"]
    if kind == "prose":
        return html_to_content(form["content_html"]).model_dump(mode="json")
    if kind == "table":
        return {"chapter_type": "table", "columns": form["columns"]}
    if kind == "stories":
        return {"chapter_type": "stories", "group_by": form["group_by"]}
    return {
        "chapter_type": "calc",
        "rows": [
            {"label": BOUND_FIELDS[field], "field": field}
            for field in form["fields"]
            if field in BOUND_FIELDS
        ],
    }


class BlockAdminState(rx.State):
    """Admins create, change, deactivate and delete chapter blocks."""

    blocks: rx.Field[list[dict[str, Any]]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    editor_open: rx.Field[bool] = rx.field(False)
    creating: rx.Field[bool] = rx.field(False)
    key: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    title: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    chapter_type: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("prose")
    level: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("1")
    guiding_question: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    content_rules: rx.Field[list[str]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    prompt_text: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    required_info: rx.Field[list[str]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    checks: rx.Field[list[str]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    active: rx.Field[bool] = rx.field(True)
    content_html: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    columns: rx.Field[list[str]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    group_by: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("activity")
    fields: rx.Field[list[str]] = rx.field(default_factory=list)
    editor_nonce: rx.Field[int] = rx.field(0)

    @rx.var
    def used_in(self) -> list[str]:
        block = next((b for b in self.blocks if b["key"] == self.key), {})
        return block.get("used_in", [])

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def load_blocks(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        try:
            self.blocks = await chapter_blocks.list_blocks(get_asyncdb_session)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Loading the chapter blocks failed")
            yield rx.toast.error(LOAD_ERROR, position="top-right")

    def _fill(self, block: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        content = parse_content(block["default_content"])
        self.key = block["key"]
        self.title = block["title"]
        self.chapter_type = block["chapter_type"]
        self.level = str(block["level"])
        self.guiding_question = block["guiding_question"]
        self.content_rules = list(block["content_rules"])
        self.prompt_text = block["prompt_text"]
        self.required_info = list(block["required_info"])
        self.checks = list(block["checks"])
        self.active = block["active"]
        self.content_html = (
            content_to_html(content) if isinstance(content, ProseContent) else ""
        )
        self.columns = list(getattr(content, "columns", DEFAULT_COLUMNS))
        self.group_by = getattr(content, "group_by", "activity")
        self.fields = [row.field for row in getattr(content, "rows", [])]
        self.editor_nonce += 1
        self.editor_open = True

    @rx.event
    def open_create(self) -> None:
        self.creating = True
        self._fill(
            {
                "key": "",
                "title": "",
                "chapter_type": "prose",
                "level": 1,
                "default_content": {"chapter_type": "prose"},
                "guiding_question": "",
                "content_rules": [],
                "prompt_text": "",
                "required_info": [],
                "checks": [],
                "active": True,
            }
        )

    @rx.event
    def open_edit(self, key: str) -> None:
        block = next((b for b in self.blocks if b["key"] == key), None)
        if block is not None:
            self.creating = False
            self._fill(block)

    @rx.event
    def close_editor(self) -> None:
        self.editor_open = False

    @rx.event
    def set_field(self, name: str, value: Any) -> None:
        """One form field; only the known ones of the editor are set."""
        if name in FORM_FIELDS:
            setattr(self, name, value)

    def _form(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {name: getattr(self, name) for name in FORM_FIELDS}

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def save(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        form = self._form()
        try:
            data = {
                **form,
                "level": int(form["level"]),
                "default_content": _start_content(form),
            }
            block = parse_block(data)
            await chapter_blocks.save_block(
                get_asyncdb_session, block, create=self.creating
            )
            self.blocks = await chapter_blocks.list_blocks(get_asyncdb_session)
        except ContentValidationError as exc:
            yield rx.toast.error(" ".join(exc.messages), position="top-right")
            return
        except BlockError as exc:
            yield rx.toast.error(str(exc), position="top-right")
            return
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Saving chapter block %s failed", form["key"])
            yield rx.toast.error(SAVE_ERROR, position="top-right")
            return
        self.editor_open = False
        yield rx.toast.success(SAVED, position="top-right")

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def delete(self, key: str) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        try:
            await chapter_blocks.delete_block(get_asyncdb_session, key)
            self.blocks = await chapter_blocks.list_blocks(get_asyncdb_session)
        except BlockError as exc:
            yield rx.toast.error(str(exc), position="top-right")
            return
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Deleting chapter block %s failed", key)
            yield rx.toast.error(SAVE_ERROR, position="top-right")
            return
        self.editor_open = False
        yield rx.toast.success(DELETED, position="top-right")


FORM_FIELDS = (
    "key",
    "title",
    "chapter_type",
    "level",
    "guiding_question",
    "content_rules",
    "prompt_text",
    "required_info",
    "checks",
    "active",
    "content_html",
    "columns",
    "group_by",
    "fields",
)
        return await active_prompt(session, name)


class PromptError(ValueError):
    """The prompt cannot be changed; the message is German."""


def _known(name: str) -> str:
    if name not in PROMPT_NAMES:
        raise PromptError(UNKNOWN_PROMPT)
    return name


async def list_prompts(sessions: SessionFactory) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every prompt name with its active version and text."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(select(PromptEntity).where(PromptEntity.active))
        ).all()
    active = {row.name: row for row in rows}
    return [
        {
            "name": name,
            "label": PROMPT_LABELS[name],
            "version": active[name].version if name in active else 0,
            "text": active[name].text if name in active else "",
        }
        for name in PROMPT_NAMES
    ]


async def prompt_versions(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Versions newest first, each with its line diff to the one before."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(
                select(PromptEntity)
                .where(PromptEntity.name == _known(name))
                .order_by(PromptEntity.version)
            )
        ).all()
    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    before: list[str] | None = None
    for row in rows:
        lines = row.text.splitlines()
        diff = [] if before is None else diff_lines(before, lines)
        entries.append(
            {
                "version": row.version,
                "active": row.active,
                "author": row.author,
                "created": row.created.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"),
                "first": before is None,
                "diff": [d for d in diff if d["kind"] != "same"],
            }
        )
        before = lines
    return entries[::-1]


async def _activate(session: AsyncSession, name: str, version: int) -> None:
    # The old version goes first: one active version per name is unique.
    await session.execute(
        update(PromptEntity)
        .where(PromptEntity.name == name, PromptEntity.active)
        .values(active=False)
    )
    await session.flush()
    await session.execute(
        update(PromptEntity)
        .where(PromptEntity.name == name, PromptEntity.version == version)
        .values(active=True)
    )


async def save_prompt(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str, text: str, user: str) -> int:
    """Store ``text`` as the next version and make it active; returns its number."""
    body = text.strip()
    if not body or len(body) > MAX_TEXT:
        raise PromptError(EMPTY_TEXT)
    async with sessions() as session:
        version = (
            await session.scalar(
                select(func.max(PromptEntity.version)).where(
                    PromptEntity.name == _known(name)
                )
            )
            or 0
        ) + 1
        session.add(
            PromptEntity(
                name=name, version=version, text=body, active=False, author=user
            )
        )
        await session.flush()
        await _activate(session, name, version)
    logger.info("Prompt %s saved as version %s", name, version)
    return version


async def activate_prompt(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str, version: int) -> None:
    async with sessions() as session:
        found = await session.scalar(
            select(PromptEntity.id).where(
                PromptEntity.name == _known(name), PromptEntity.version == version
            )
        )
        if found is None:
            raise PromptError(UNKNOWN_VERSION)
        await _activate(session, name, version)
    logger.info("Prompt %s version %s activated", name, version)

    @rx.event

    "key",
    "title",
    "chapter_type",
