class PromptError(ValueError):
    """The prompt cannot be changed; the message is German."""


def _known(name: str) -> str:
    if name not in PROMPT_NAMES:
        raise PromptError(UNKNOWN_PROMPT)
    return name


async def list_prompts(sessions: SessionFactory) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Every prompt name with its active version and text."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(select(PromptEntity).where(PromptEntity.active))
        ).all()
    active = {row.name: row for row in rows}
    return [
        {
            "name": name,
            "label": PROMPT_LABELS[name],
            "version": active[name].version if name in active else 0,
            "text": active[name].text if name in active else "",
        }
        for name in PROMPT_NAMES
    ]


async def prompt_versions(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Versions newest first, each with its line diff to the one before."""
    async with sessions() as session:
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(
                select(PromptEntity)
                .where(PromptEntity.name == _known(name))
                .order_by(PromptEntity.version)
            )
        ).all()
    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    before: list[str] | None = None
    for row in rows:
        lines = row.text.splitlines()
        diff = [] if before is None else diff_lines(before, lines)
        entries.append(
            {
                "version": row.version,
                "active": row.active,
                "author": row.author,
                "created": row.created.strftime("%d.%m.%Y %H:%M"),
                "first": before is None,
                "diff": [d for d in diff if d["kind"] != "same"],
            }
        )
        before = lines
    return entries[::-1]


async def _activate(session: AsyncSession, name: str, version: int) -> None:
    # The old version goes first: one active version per name is unique.
    await session.execute(
        update(PromptEntity)
        .where(PromptEntity.name == name, PromptEntity.active)
        .values(active=False)
    )
    await session.flush()
    await session.execute(
        update(PromptEntity)
        .where(PromptEntity.name == name, PromptEntity.version == version)
        .values(active=True)
    )


async def save_prompt(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str, text: str, user: str) -> int:
    """Store ``text`` as the next version and make it active; returns its number."""
    body = text.strip()
    if not body or len(body) > MAX_TEXT:
        raise PromptError(EMPTY_TEXT)
    async with sessions() as session:
        version = (
            await session.scalar(
                select(func.max(PromptEntity.version)).where(
                    PromptEntity.name == _known(name)
                )
            )
            or 0
        ) + 1
        session.add(
            PromptEntity(
                name=name, version=version, text=body, active=False, author=user
            )
        )
        await session.flush()
        await _activate(session, name, version)
    logger.info("Prompt %s saved as version %s", name, version)
    return version


async def activate_prompt(sessions: SessionFactory, name: str, version: int) -> None:
    async with sessions() as session:
        found = await session.scalar(
            select(PromptEntity.id).where(
                PromptEntity.name == _known(name), PromptEntity.version == version
            )
        )
        if found is None:
            raise PromptError(UNKNOWN_VERSION)
        await _activate(session, name, version)
    logger.info("Prompt %s version %s activated", name, version)

async def test_outline_entries_are_added_moved_changed_and_removed(db) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    template_id = await _template_id(db)
    draft = TemplateDraft(db.session, template_id)
    await chapter_blocks.save_block(db.session, parse_block(BLOCK), create=True)
    await draft.add_block("datenschutz")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.BLOCK_IN_OUTLINE):
        await draft.add_block("datenschutz")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.NO_BLOCK):
        await draft.add_block("gibt_es_nicht")
    outline = await template_drafts.load_outline(db.session, template_id)
    added = outline[-1]
    assert (added["block_key"], added["level"], added["required"]) == (
        "datenschutz",
        2,
        False,
    )
    await draft.move(added["id"], 0)
    await draft.update(added["id"], required=True, title=" Schutz ", level=1)
    outline = await template_drafts.load_outline(db.session, template_id)
    assert (outline[0]["title"], outline[0]["level"], outline[0]["required"]) == (
        "Schutz",
        1,
        True,
    )
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.BAD_LEVEL):
        await draft.update(added["id"], required=True, title="", level=3)
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.TITLE_TOO_LONG):
        await draft.update(added["id"], required=True, title="x" * 256, level=None)
    await draft.remove(added["id"])
    outline = await template_drafts.load_outline(db.session, template_id)
    assert outline[0]["block_key"] == "management_summary"
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.NO_ENTRY):
        await draft.remove(added["id"])
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.NOT_FOUND):
        await TemplateDraft(db.session, 999).add_block("laufzeit")


async def test_layout_upload_is_checked_cleaned_and_reads_the_frame(db) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    template_id = await _template_id(db)
    draft = TemplateDraft(db.session, template_id)
    store = DbBlobStore(10_000_000, db.session)
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match="Word"):
        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.pdf", b"%PDF")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match="Word"):
        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.docx", b"kein zip")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match="Anker"):
        document = Document()
        out = io.BytesIO()
        document.save(out)
        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.docx", out.getvalue())
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.TOO_LARGE):
        await draft.upload_layout(DbBlobStore(10, db.session), "l.docx", _layout())
    await draft.upload_layout(store, "Layout.DOCX", _layout("Hinweis"))
    templates = await template_drafts.list_templates(db.session)
    assert (templates[0]["frame_before"], templates[0]["frame_after"]) == (
        ["Hinweis"],
        ["Unterschriften"],
    )
    assert templates[0]["latest"] == 1


async def test_publish_makes_the_next_version_for_new_offers_only(db) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    async with db.session() as session:
        await open_workspace(session, 1, "Anna")
    template_id = await _template_id(db)
    draft = TemplateDraft(db.session, template_id)
    await chapter_blocks.save_block(db.session, parse_block(BLOCK), create=True)
    await draft.add_block("datenschutz")
    await draft.upload_layout(
        DbBlobStore(10_000_000, db.session), "layout.docx", _layout("Hinweis")
    )
    assert await draft.publish("Admin") == 2
    versions = await template_drafts.list_versions(db.session, template_id)
    assert (versions[0]["number"], versions[0]["published_by"]) == (2, "Admin")
    async with db.session() as session:
        latest = await latest_template(session, "quo_v1")
    assert latest.version == "2"
    assert latest.chapters[-1].key == "datenschutz"
    assert latest.chapters[-1].prompt_text == "Nenne die DSGVO."
    assert latest.frame_before == ["Hinweis"]
    # The offer made before keeps version 1 and its own outline.
    keys = [c["key"] for c in await ChapterService(db.session, 1, "Anna").open()]
    assert "datenschutz" not in keys


async def test_publish_needs_a_layout_and_chapters(db) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    async with db.session() as session:
        template = OfferTemplateEntity(key="leer", name="Leer")
        session.add(template)
        await session.flush()
        template_id = template.id
    draft = TemplateDraft(db.session, template_id)
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.NO_LAYOUT):
        await draft.publish("Admin")
    await draft.upload_layout(DbBlobStore(10_000_000, db.session), "l.docx", _layout())
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.EMPTY_OUTLINE):
        await draft.publish("Admin")

        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.pdf", b"%PDF")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match="Word"):
        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.docx", b"kein zip")
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match="Anker"):
        document = Document()
        out = io.BytesIO()
        document.save(out)
        await draft.upload_layout(store, "layout.docx", out.getvalue())
    with pytest.raises(DraftError, match=template_drafts.TOO_LARGE):
        await draft.upload_layout(DbBlobStore(10, db.session), "l.docx", _layout())

async def test_publish_makes_the_next_version_for_new_offers_only(db) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    async with db.session() as session:
        await open_workspace(session, 1, "Anna")
    template_id = await _template_id(db)
    draft = TemplateDraft(db.session, template_id)
    await chapter_blocks.save_block(db.session, parse_block(BLOCK), create=True)
    await draft.add_block("datenschutz")
    await draft.upload_layout(
        DbBlobStore(10_000_000, db.session), "layout.docx", _layout("Hinweis")
    )
    assert await draft.publish("Admin") == 2
    versions = await template_drafts.list_versions(db.session, template_id)
    assert (versions[0]["number"], versions[0]["published_by"]) == (2, "Admin")
    async with db.session() as session:
        latest = await latest_template(session, "quo_v1")
    assert latest.version == "2"
    assert latest.chapters[-1].key == "datenschutz"
    assert latest.chapters[-1].prompt_text == "Nenne die DSGVO."
    assert latest.frame_before == ["Hinweis"]
    # The offer made before keeps version 1 and its own outline.
    keys = [c["key"] for c in await ChapterService(db.session, 1, "Anna").open()]
    assert "datenschutz" not in keys

    async with db.session() as session:

        await draft.publish("Admin")

feat(offer): add the "Angebote" admin menu for templates, blocks and prompts

The new page /admin/offers has three tabs:
- Vorlagen: admins edit the draft outline (add, remove and drag entries, set
  title, level and required flag), upload a Word layout and publish it as the
  next immutable version. New offers use that version; existing offers keep
  theirs. Publishing an unchanged draft is refused.
- Kapitelbausteine: admins create, change, deactivate and delete chapter
  blocks with their settings and start content. Blocks used in a template
  cannot be deleted.
- Prompts: admins save a new version of an AI prompt or activate an older
  one, with a line diff per version. The fixed data guard stays in front of
  every prompt.

Uploaded layouts are size-checked as a zip before parsing (total, per XML
part, part count). They are cleaned of comments, tracked changes (also format
changes and moved text), authors, the thumbnail and private properties. A
replaced draft layout is deleted when no version uses it. Every handler is
admin-only.

Shared code: one helper parses numbers sent by the browser, and the author
name comes from current_user_name.

Deviations from the plan:
- Template drafts are service functions and a TemplateDraft class instead of
  a TemplateService.
- Admins cannot create new templates yet; they edit the seeded one.
- Only the prose start content uses the chapter editor. Table, stories and
  calc blocks use simple fields.
- The sidebar shows "Angebote" twice: once in planning, once in the
  administration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

# Offer workshop template (QUO)

The workshop fills the customer template `Templates/QUO-33441-N7R0Z4_Preisindikation MVP Referenzdatenbank Treystar .docx`.
`scripts/inventory_docx.py` prints its structure; `scripts/build_quo_layout.py` turns it into the layout.
The template lives in the database: the migration `2026_10_31_offer_templates.py` seeds template `quo_v1` as published version 1, with its chapter blocks and the layout from `alembic/seed/quo_v1_layout.docx` as a blob.

## What is fixed and what is generated

| Part | Source in the QUO file | In the package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover (title, customer, date, quote id) | paragraphs 0 to 25 | the layout with `{{ project_title }}`, `{{ customer_name }}`, `{{ customer_street }}`, `{{ customer_city }}`, `{{ customer_short }}`, `{{ offer_date }}`, `{{ quote_id }}` |
| Legal notice, supplier address | cover | fixed text |
| Table of contents | missing in the QUO file | TOC field `1-3`, updated when Word opens the file |
| Chapters Management Summary to Consumption | Heading 1 to 3 | removed from the layout, rendered from typed chapters at the anchor `[[KAPITEL]]` |
| Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist (`{{ validity_date }}`), Sonstiges, Anlagen, Unterschriften | tail | fixed text; signature placeholders (`$$_PRT_..._$$`) stay untouched |

Customer data, reviewer comments, people, labels and author names are removed from the layout. There is no story map chapter: the document shows written stories only.

## Chapters of version 1

| Key | Level | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `management_summary` | 1 | prose | yes |
| `leistungen` | 1 | prose | no |
| `user_stories` | 2 | stories (all live stories, grouped by activity) | yes |
| `loesung` | 2 | prose | yes |
| `leistungsumfang` | 2 | prose | yes |
| `mitwirkung` | 2 | table (Mitwirkung, Verantwortlich, Zeitpunkt) | yes |
| `rahmenbedingungen` | 2 | prose | no |
| `projektabwicklung` | 1 | prose | no |
| `laufzeit` | 1 | prose | yes |
| `verguetung` | 1 | calc (person days, risk buffer, production cost, recommended price) | yes |
| `annahmen_risiken` | 1 | prose | no |

The consumption chapter of the QUO file is not part of Etappe 1.

## Word styles used by the renderer

| Content | Style |
| --- | --- |
| Chapter titles | `Heading 1` and `Heading 2` (style ids `berschrift1`, `berschrift2`) |
| Headings inside a chapter | `Heading 3`, `Heading 4`, never above the chapter level |
| Text | `Normal` |
| Bullet list | `Aufzählung 1` |
| Ordered list | `List Number` |
| Tables | table style `arvato-Tabelle blau`, header row repeats |

## Rendering rules

- Content is rendered by one renderer per chapter type; unknown content raises a typed error and is never dropped.
- `stories` chapters list the stories of the bound map revision: a heading per group, then key and title, then the one sentence "Als … möchte ich …, um …".
- `calc` values are shown only when confirmed; an unconfirmed value carries `[nicht bestätigt]`, a missing one `[Wert fehlt]`.
- A draft export starts with the marker "ENTWURF – nicht zur Weitergabe an den Kunden".
- `docs/features/offer-workshop-sample.docx` is a reference export for the manual check in Word.

# Offer workshop

The workshop is the page `/offers/<id>/werkstatt` ("Angebotswerkstatt"). It belongs to the package `alloq-offer`, lives in `alloq_offer/workshop/` and is open only to the role `offer_editor`. Other roles, administrators included, get no workshop data and cannot run any workshop action. The tests `test_workshop_authorization.py` and `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforce this for every handler.

The planning background is in [spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md](../../spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md). The Word template is described in [Offer workshop template](./offer-workshop-template.md). Offers themselves are described in [Offers](./offers.md).

## User flow

1. **Open the workshop** from an offer. The workspace is created on the first visit and bound to the current template version.
2. **Add sources** in the tab "Entwurf" (right column): pasted text, EML, TXT, DOCX, PDF, PPTX and audio. Each source shows its status and its gaps, a progress bar shows how many sources are read, and "Ansehen" lists the extracted blocks with their place (page, paragraph, slide, time) (scanned pages, pictures, audio that needs a transcript). Identical content adds nothing, changed content with the same file name becomes a new version. A source can be withdrawn; see below.
3. **Create the first draft.** One click on "Entwurf aus N Quellen erzeugen" runs a chain of jobs: story map and briefing, then every prose chapter (kept as revision), then the AI review and the first Word draft. With "Automatisch entwerfen" the chain starts by itself once a source is usable; with an existing map a new source only gives a map proposal. The tab "Entwurf" shows each stage with a progress bar, then a summary with the download of the Word draft and the list "Braucht Ihre Entscheidung" (open points in the briefing, calculation, blockers). Stories are simple sentences "Als ..., möchte ich ..., um ..." and never carry acceptance criteria. Every live story on the map is part of the offer; to leave a story out, archive it.
4. **Edit the map** in the tab "Story Map". Add, rename, reorder, split and archive activities, tasks and stories and move stories between slices. Every write names the map revision it expects; a stale write is refused and the current map is shown. The AI can also propose missing process steps or a split of the selected story. Such a proposal is shown as a comparison, is bound to the map revision it was made for, becomes "veraltet" when the map changed, and adds only new elements when taken over.
5. **Read the briefing.** Statements are grouped by type. Conflicts show both sources. "Als fachliche Entscheidung bestätigen" is a separate, explicit action.
6. **Write the chapters.** The editor saves automatically against the revision it started from. Each save is a new revision with history, diff and restore. AI proposals appear as a comparison and change nothing until a person accepts them. A protected chapter is never changed by the AI.
7. **Check.** Rule checks run when the tab opens. The AI review adds remarks, but never edits content and cannot raise a blocker. Blockers cannot be accepted, other findings only with a reason.
8. **Confirm the calculation.** The values come from the offer. Any later change voids the confirmation and flags the chapters that show the values.
9. **Export.** The tab "Export" creates a Word draft at any time, and a final version once no blocker is open, the calculation is confirmed (when a price is required) and the person confirms the whole state. Each file is made from a fixed snapshot. Changes made later in Word are not taken back into the workshop.

## Output kinds

| Kind | Allowed when | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entwurf | Always | Visible draft marker, open points at the end |
| Final | No open blocker, confirmed calculation if a price is required, confirmation of the whole state | No draft marker, no internal review notes |

## Source withdrawal

Withdrawing a source (trash button in the source list) blocks its use at once. The extracted blocks and the stored file are deleted, the file only when no other source uses the same content. All versions of the same file are withdrawn together. Briefing statements that cite the source get the mark "needs recheck", the written chapters are flagged for review, and the check `source_revoked` lists every story and statement that still cites the deleted blocks.

## Architecture

| Layer | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entities and migrations | `workshop/entities.py`, `alembic/versions/2026_10_2*` | One migration per phase; the user applies them |
| Storage | `workshop/storage.py` | `BlobStore` port, files in Postgres once per SHA-256 |
| Jobs | `workshop/jobs/` | Own persistent queue with lease, retries and idempotency keys; handlers register by kind |
| Extraction | `workshop/extraction/` | One pure parser per source kind |
| AI | `workshop/ai/` | pydantic-ai agents on Azure OpenAI behind a port, versioned prompts, sources passed as delimited data |
| Services | `workshop/services/` | Map, chapters, checks, findings, commercials, snapshots, exports, source withdrawal |
| Content | `workshop/content/` | Canonical content tree and editor conversion; unsupported markup is reported, not dropped |
| Export | `workshop/export/` | Template package of a published version (`services/templates.py`), Word renderer, structural check |
| States and components | `workshop/states/`, `workshop/components/` | One state per tab |

Jobs run in the worker task started with the app when `app.offer_workshop.worker_enabled` is true. Without it, uploaded sources stay "hochgeladen" and no draft or export is made. Server and desktop can both run it, because jobs are claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.

The chain of the first draft lives in `services/draft_pipeline.py`. Each stage is its own job, so a failed stage is retried alone and the stages before it stay saved.

`app.offer_workshop.ai_provider` selects the model: `azure` (default) or `demo`. The demo provider (`ai/demo.py`) needs no language model: stories, statements and chapter text quote sentences of the sources and cite their blocks. The local profile uses it together with the worker. `scripts/seed_workshop_demo.py` creates a complete demo offer with five sources in the configured database.

### Export flow

1. The state refuses the request while the chapter editor shows an unsaved or conflicting change.
2. The service runs the rule checks on the current state and, for the final version, collects every reason (open blockers, unconfirmed calculation, missing confirmation).
3. It stores an immutable snapshot (chapters with their revision numbers, resolved stories and values, cover data, open points) and queues the job `export_docx`.
4. The job renders the snapshot with the template version stored in the snapshot, checks the file (chapter headings in order, draft marker fits the kind), stores it and writes the manifest: snapshot, map revision, template and exporter version, chapter revisions, checksum, size.
5. The download returns exactly the stored bytes and refuses a file whose checksum changed. A failed job leaves the export marked as failed with a retry by a new request; the saved offer is untouched.

A template version that is no longer available stops the export with a clear message, so an offer keeps its bound version until it is migrated on purpose.

## Operations

- Telemetry: the worker logs one line per job attempt with kind, outcome, duration and error class, and one line per model call with the number of requests and tokens. Source text, prompts and chapter content are never logged.
- Configuration: see `WorkshopConfig` in `workshop/configuration.py` (limits, worker, Azure OpenAI). The API key is a secret reference.
- Tables: `offer_workspaces`, `offer_blobs`, `offer_jobs`, `offer_sources`, `offer_source_blocks`, `offer_activities`, `offer_tasks`, `offer_stories`, `offer_slices`, `offer_statements`, `offer_map_revisions`, `offer_generation_runs`, `offer_chapters`, `offer_chapter_revisions`, `offer_proposals`, `offer_findings`, `offer_snapshots`, `offer_exports`.

## Tests

`components/alloq-offer/tests/test_workshop_acceptance.py` maps the acceptance cases A01 to A27 of the spec to the tests that prove them and fails when a proof disappears. One check cannot be automated: open an exported file in Word and look at layout, table of contents (fields update on open), headers and footers.

The workshop is the page `/offers/<id>/werkstatt` ("Angebotswerkstatt"). It belongs to the package `alloq-offer`, lives in `alloq_offer/workshop/` and is open only to the role `offer_editor`. Other roles, administrators included, get no workshop data and cannot run any workshop action. The tests `test_workshop_authorization.py` and `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforce this for every handler.

-The planning background is in [spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md](../../spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md). The Word template is described in [Offer workshop template](./offer-workshop-template.md). Offers themselves are described in [Offers](./offers.md).

3. **Create the first draft.** One click on "Entwurf aus N Quellen erzeugen" runs a chain of jobs: story map and briefing, then every prose chapter (kept as revision), then the AI review and the first Word draft. With "Automatisch entwerfen" the chain starts by itself once a source is usable; with an existing map a new source only gives a map proposal. The tab "Entwurf" shows each stage with a progress bar, then a summary with the download of the Word draft and the list "Braucht Ihre Entscheidung" (open points in the briefing, calculation, blockers). Stories are simple sentences "Als ..., möchte ich ..., um ..." and never carry acceptance criteria. Every live story on the map is part of the offer; to leave a story out, archive it.

4. **Edit the map** in the tab "Story Map". Add, rename, reorder, split and archive activities, tasks and stories and move stories between slices. Every write names the map revision it expects; a stale write is refused and the current map is shown. The AI can also propose missing process steps or a split of the selected story. Such a proposal is shown as a comparison, is bound to the map revision it was made for, becomes "veraltet" when the map changed, and adds only new elements when taken over.
5. **Read the briefing.** Statements are grouped by type. Conflicts show both sources. "Als fachliche Entscheidung bestätigen" is a separate, explicit action.

-6. **Write the chapters.** The editor saves automatically against the revision it started from. Each save is a new revision with history, diff and restore. AI proposals appear as a comparison and change nothing until a person accepts them. A protected chapter is never changed by the AI.

+6. **Write the chapters.** The tab "Kapitel" shows the offer as one document with an outline on the left and a panel for the selected chapter on the right. Only the selected chapter shows its toolbar, which floats over the chapter's top edge. The outline follows the rules in "Outline" below. The editor saves automatically against the revision it started from. Each save is a new revision with history, diff and restore. AI proposals appear as a comparison and change nothing until a person accepts them. A protected chapter is never changed by the AI.
7. **Check.** Rule checks run when the tab opens. The AI review adds remarks, but never edits content and cannot raise a blocker. Blockers cannot be accepted, other findings only with a reason.
8. **Confirm the calculation.** The values come from the offer. Any later change voids the confirmation and flags the chapters that show the values.

9. **Export.** The tab "Export" creates a Word draft at any time, and a final version once no blocker is open, the calculation is confirmed (when a price is required) and the person confirms the whole state. Each file is made from a fixed snapshot. Changes made later in Word are not taken back into the workshop.
+Each offer has its own outline, copied from the template version it is bound to.

+- **Add.** "+ Kapitel" adds a block from the library with its start content and settings, or a blank chapter of type prose, table, stories or calc. A block can be in the outline only once. An offer has at most 100 chapters.

+- **Remove and restore.** Required chapters cannot be removed. A removed chapter keeps its revisions, findings and proposals and can be restored. A restored chapter is flagged for review. Findings of removed chapters are not shown until the chapter comes back.

+- **Order.** Chapters are dragged in the outline, by mouse or by keyboard (space to pick up, arrow keys to move, space to drop). The fixed frame of the layout is not part of the outline and never moves.

+- **Title and level.** Each chapter can be renamed and set to level 1 (Kapitel) or 2 (Unterkapitel). The first chapter always has level 1. The numbers (1, 2, 2.1, 3) follow position and level, in the workshop and in Word.
+- **Export.** Word shows the chapters in outline order with their titles and levels. Removed chapters are left out.
+All outline changes need the role `offer_editor` and are refused for archived offers.
| Services | `workshop/services/` | Map, chapters, checks, findings, commercials, snapshots, exports, source withdrawal |
| Content | `workshop/content/` | Canonical content tree and editor conversion; unsupported markup is reported, not dropped |
| Export | `workshop/export/` | Template package of a published version (`services/templates.py`), Word renderer, structural check |
+| Outline | `services/outline.py`, `services/numbering.py` | Add, remove, restore, move, rename and re-level chapters; numbering |
+| Admin | `alloq_offer/admin/`, `services/template_drafts.py`, `services/chapter_blocks.py`, `services/prompts.py` | Page `/admin/offers` with the tabs Vorlagen, Kapitelbausteine and Prompts |
| States and components | `workshop/states/`, `workshop/components/` | One state per tab |

Jobs run in the worker task started with the app when `app.offer_workshop.worker_enabled` is true. Without it, uploaded sources stay "hochgeladen" and no draft or export is made. Server and desktop can both run it, because jobs are claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`.

- Telemetry: the worker logs one line per job attempt with kind, outcome, duration and error class, and one line per model call with the number of requests and tokens. Source text, prompts and chapter content are never logged.
- Configuration: see `WorkshopConfig` in `workshop/configuration.py` (limits, worker, Azure OpenAI). The API key is a secret reference.

---
name: sortable-list-reflex-keys
description: hello-pangea dnd in Reflex (alloq_commons sortable) needs one SortableItem per foreach row, key=item_id and a version prop
metadata:
  type: project
---

`alloq_commons/components/sortable.py` wraps `@hello-pangea/dnd` for drag lists (Kapitel outline, admin template outline). Three traps found on 2026-10-26:

- Reflex memoizes an `rx.foreach` into one child, so a Draggable around the foreach showed the whole list as one item. Render `sortable_item(...)` inside the foreach, one per row.
- Foreach keys rows by index. After a reorder dnd's registry pointed at stale nodes ("Unable to find draggable"). `sortable_item` sets `key=item_id`.
- The list shows an interim order after a drop. Bump a state `order_version` after every move answer (also on failure) and pass it as `version`, or a refused move stays visible.

**Why:** each cost a debugging round in the browser.
**How to apply:** copy the outline usage (`OutlineMixin.order_version`, `TemplateAdminState.order_version`) for any new sortable list.

---
name: sortable-list-reflex-keys
description: hello-pangea dnd in Reflex (alloq_commons sortable) needs one SortableItem per foreach row, key=item_id and a version prop
metadata:
  type: project
---

`alloq_commons/components/sortable.py` wraps `@hello-pangea/dnd` for drag lists (Kapitel outline, admin template outline). Three traps found on 2026-10-26:

- Reflex memoizes an `rx.foreach` into one child, so a Draggable around the foreach showed the whole list as one item. Render `sortable_item(...)` inside the foreach, one per row.
- Foreach keys rows by index. After a reorder dnd's registry pointed at stale nodes ("Unable to find draggable"). `sortable_item` sets `key=item_id`.
- The list shows an interim order after a drop. Bump a state `order_version` after every move answer (also on failure) and pass it as `version`, or a refused move stays visible.

**Why:** each cost a debugging round in the browser.
**How to apply:** copy the outline usage (`OutlineMixin.order_version`, `TemplateAdminState.order_version`) for any new sortable list.

files.content:
- [uv env is .venv.mac](uv-project-environment-venv-mac.md) — UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT points to .venv.mac; .venv is stale
- [Local test login](local-test-login.md) — alloq admin test account for localhost visual checks only
- [Reflex mixin, not substate](reflex-mixin-not-substate.md) — list logic for big states lives in mixins; substates break standalone-state tests
- [Hot reload after state changes](reflex-hot-reload-new-state.md) — 'reading length' crash means reload + re-login, not a bug
- [Postgres Entra login infra](postgres-entra-login-infra.md) — desktop DB access: infra in knowledgeai-container, role via migration, grants on desktop users page
- [tauri-dev window effects](tauri-dev-window-effects.md) — desktop:dev scaffold needs vibrancy settings hand-added like tauri/
- [Reflex render escapes umlauts](reflex-render-escapes-umlauts.md) — str(component) shows ä as ä; assert on constants
- [Local visual check browser](local-visual-check-browser.md) — chrome-devtools isolated context reaches localhost; pane and Playwright didn't
- [Theme is macOS blue](alloq-theme-macos-blue.md) — colors from alloq_commons/theme.py; the Alloq design-system artifact is outdated teal
- [Planning header width](planning-header-needs-table-width.md) — sticky grid headers need table width or bg ends at viewport
- [de_number ignores text props](de-number-ignores-text-props.md) — wrap de_number in mn.text for fz/c/fw
- [Access levels](employee-role-read-only.md) — role-only: admin switch = admin menu + price list edits; employee reads, project_manager edits (needs employee too); fakes need roles
- [Split: keep DB code in place](split-keep-db-handlers-in-place.md) — tests patch MODULE.repo; move only UI-only/pure code out of big files
- [mn max_length is CSS](mantine-max-length-is-css.md) — use custom_attrs={"maxLength": N} for a real browser limit
- [scroll_area h is not CSS](mn-scroll-area-h-not-css.md) — mn.scroll_area h= does nothing; use style={"height": ...}
- [rx.LocalStorage lost on login](rx-localstorage-lost-on-login.md) — appkit-user 1.16.1 bug (hydrate_and_load + terminate reset); fixed in appkit source, unreleased
- [Dialogs over popovers](mantine-z-index-layers.md) — page popovers use theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX (150) so dialogs (200) cover them
- [Layout CSS in assets](layout-css-in-assets.md) — static CSS in assets/css/aq-*.css, not Python strings
- [Big jobs page by page](big-jobs-page-by-page.md) — one agent per page with a progress file; parallel workflows hit the session limit
- [Password tables unmigrated](appkit-user-password-tables-unmigrated.md) — appkit_user password tables on metadata have no Alembic migration
- [Docs diagram style](docs-diagram-style.md) — draw.io dev-docs look, facts from the page, no duplication
- [NumberInput blur value](mantine-number-input-blur-value.md) — on_blur sends "1.120 €" text; key uncontrolled inputs by derived values
- [Offers package and role](offer-package-and-role.md) — all users read (appkit @is_authenticated), only offer_editor edits (not admins); UI uses appkit requires_role, no has_role exists
- [Project eager history](project-entity-eager-history.md) — ProjectEntity selectin-loads all allocations; planning uses find_all_for_planning
- [Project dates no staffing limit](project-dates-no-staffing-limit.md) — allocations before start / after end still count as team
- [Umlauts sort after Z](postgres-umlaut-sort-order.md) — Postgres ORDER BY name puts Ö last; sort German names in Python (NFKD key)
- [Local profile uses remote DB](local-profile-remote-db.md) — PROFILES=local hits a shared .tech Postgres; never run alembic yourself
- [rx.icon renders as Lucide name](rx-icon-renders-as-lucide-name.md) — str() shows LucideX, not the kebab name; assert on that
- [Router page deprecated](reflex-router-page-deprecated.md) — read route segment from router.url.path, not router.page.params
- [Alembic blocked by hook](alembic-blocked-by-hook.md) — hook refuses upgrade even on user request; hand over the command
- [Post-edit hook autofix](post-edit-hook-autofix.md) — import + use in one Edit; Literal as module alias
- [Workshop local demo AI](workshop-local-demo-ai.md) — local: worker on + ai_provider demo; seed script, demo offer 5
- [Mantine beats plain classes](mantine-class-position-override.md) — compound .mantine-X-root in selectors; no transform centering (:active replaces it)
- [Workshop tests vs real clock](workshop-tests-real-clock.md) — jobs queue follow-ups with now(); fixed-NOW tests break after that date
- [Viewer rail only >1 page](workshop-viewer-rail-single-page.md) — source viewer port from mail-archive; demo PDF/DOCX are one page so no rail
- [Shared asset folder per module](reflex-shared-asset-folder-per-module.md) — rx.asset(shared=True) folder = calling module; co-importing JS must share it
- [Var .to(str) is a cast](reflex-var-to-str-is-a-cast.md) — compare str field with foreach int via .to_string(), not .to(str)
- [react-pptx fit mode](react-pptx-fit-mode.md) — only contain/none; "width" = none; contain needs viewport padding moved to margin
- [Form in foreach](reflex-form-in-foreach.md) — on_submit inside rx.foreach can't use loop vars; store context in state, submit plain handler
- [Blob store default session](blob-store-default-session.md) — DbBlobStore default factory hits the shared DB in tests; pass get_asyncdb_session

## What is fixed and what is generated

**Layout upload.** The file must be a `.docx` with exactly one paragraph `[[KAPITEL]]`. Headings before and after the anchor are the fixed frame. Before the file is parsed, its size as a zip is checked: at most 2000 parts, 10 MB per XML part and 100 MB unpacked in total. The stored layout is cleaned of comments, people, custom XML, custom and extended properties, the thumbnail, linked files, tracked changes (deleted and moved-away text, old formatting) and author, subject and print data. Layouts are cleaned again when a version is loaded. A replaced draft layout is deleted when no published version uses it.

-**Prompts.** Each prompt name has numbered versions and exactly one active version. The AI loads the active version once per run and records it as `name@version` in the generation run. A fixed rule about the data tags (`<quelle>`, `<map>`, `<briefing>`, `<kapitel>`, `<aktueller_text>`) always comes before the prompt text and cannot be removed in the admin menu. Admins are trusted. A prompt text that contradicts this rule weakens it, so the tab shows a warning above the text.

+**Prompts.** Each prompt name has numbered versions and exactly one active version. The AI loads the active version once per run and records it as `name@version` in the generation run. A fixed rule about the data tags of that prompt (`DATA_TAGS` in `services/prompts.py`, for example `<map>`, `<briefing>` and `<aktueller_text>` for chapters) always comes before the prompt text and cannot be removed in the admin menu. Admins are trusted. A prompt text that contradicts this rule weakens it, so the tab shows a warning above the text.
## Word styles used by the renderer
Each offer has its own outline, copied from the template version it is bound to.

- **Add.** "+ Kapitel" adds a block from the library with its start content and settings, or a blank chapter of type prose, table, stories or calc. A block can be in the outline only once. An offer has at most 100 chapters.

-- **Remove and restore.** Required chapters cannot be removed. A removed chapter keeps its revisions, findings and proposals and can be restored. A restored chapter is flagged for review. Findings of removed chapters are not shown until the chapter comes back.

+- **Remove and restore.** Required chapters cannot be removed. A removed chapter keeps its revisions, findings and proposals and can be restored. A restored chapter goes to the end of the outline and is flagged for review. Findings of removed chapters are not shown until the chapter comes back.

- **Order.** Chapters are dragged in the outline, by mouse or by keyboard (space to pick up, arrow keys to move, space to drop). The fixed frame of the layout is not part of the outline and never moves.

- **Title and level.** Each chapter can be renamed and set to level 1 (Kapitel) or 2 (Unterkapitel). The first chapter always has level 1. The numbers (1, 2, 2.1, 3) follow position and level, in the workshop and in Word.
- **Export.** Word shows the chapters in outline order with their titles and levels. Removed chapters are left out.

lines: Der Reiter „Kapitel“ zeigt das Angebot als ein Dokument. Links steht die Gliederung, rechts ein Bereich mit den Einstellungen des gewählten Kapitels. Jedes Angebot hat eine eigene Gliederung, die beim Anlegen aus der gebundenen Vorlagenversion kopiert wird. Für die Gliederung gelten diese Regeln:

- Über „+ Kapitel“ kommt ein Baustein aus der Bibliothek mit Startinhalt und Einstellungen hinzu, oder ein leeres Kapitel vom Typ Text, Tabelle, Stories oder Kalkulation. Jeder Baustein steht höchstens einmal in der Gliederung. Ein Angebot hat höchstens 100 Kapitel.

-- Pflichtkapitel lassen sich verschieben, aber nicht entfernen. Ein entferntes Kapitel behält Revisionen, Prüfhinweise und Vorschläge und lässt sich wiederherstellen. Nach dem Wiederherstellen ist es zur Prüfung markiert.

+- Pflichtkapitel lassen sich verschieben, aber nicht entfernen. Ein entferntes Kapitel behält Revisionen, Prüfhinweise und Vorschläge und lässt sich wiederherstellen. Nach dem Wiederherstellen steht es am Ende der Gliederung und ist zur Prüfung markiert.
- Kapitel werden in der Gliederung mit Maus oder Tastatur verschoben. Der feste Rahmen des Word-Layouts gehört nicht zur Gliederung und bleibt an seinem Platz.

- Jedes Kapitel hat einen eigenen Titel und die Ebene Kapitel oder Unterkapitel. Das erste Kapitel hat immer die Ebene Kapitel. Die Nummern (1, 2, 2.1, 3) ergeben sich aus Reihenfolge und Ebene, in der Werkstatt und im Word-Dokument.

The whole plan is implemented and committed to `feature/offer-doc`, one commit per phase plus two fixes. Nothing is pushed. Each phase had a code review, a security review and a simplification pass. The last full run was green: lint, type check, 2387 tests passing, 92.6 % coverage and no file over 1000 lines. After that run I only changed CSS and docs, and the admin tests still pass.

**What changed since the last update**

- **Phase 5, admin page `/admin/offers`** (d9d7436). It has three tabs:
  - **Vorlagen:** edit the draft outline, upload a Word layout and publish it as the next version.
  - **Kapitelbausteine:** create, change, deactivate and delete chapter blocks.
  - **Prompts:** save a new prompt version or activate an older one, with a diff per version.

  Every handler is admin only.
- **Code review fixes:**
  - A crafted request could overwrite a different block while editing one. The block key is now fixed in edit mode.
  - Publishing an unchanged draft no longer creates a duplicate version.
  - Two admins editing the same outline entry no longer reset each other's settings, because only the changed field is saved.
  - A save followed by a failed reload now shows a load error, not "konnte nicht gespeichert werden".
  - Two admins saving or activating the same prompt at once now get a German message instead of the generic error.
- **Security review fixes** (nothing critical or high was found):
  - Layout cleaning now also removes formatting changes, moved text, the thumbnail, the subject and the print date.
  - Upload limits are tighter: 10 MB per XML part and 100 MB unpacked in total.
  - A replaced draft layout is deleted when no published version uses it.
  - Logs no longer contain chapter text.
  - Admin form inputs now have type and size limits.
- **Simplification:** four copies of the number parsing helper became one. The admin pages reuse the existing `current_user_name`.
- **Layout fix** (4d6d15d): on narrow windows the outline title fields were squeezed to a few letters. The side panel now wraps below the outline.
- **Phase 6, docs** (51f441f): spec sections 5.5 and 6.1, the workshop and template pages, and the architecture and access pages. A docs check found eight stale places, and they are fixed.

**What you need to do**

1. Run the migration that replaces the uncleaned layout in the shared database. I am not allowed to run it:
   ```bash
   uv run alembic upgrade head
   ```
2. An earlier test run wrote three test files (blobs 13 to 15) into the shared dev database. Nothing uses them. I did not delete them without your OK. This removes them only if nothing references them:
   ```sql
   DELETE FROM offer_blobs WHERE id IN (13,14,15) AND id NOT IN (SELECT blob_id FROM offer_sources WHERE blob_id IS NOT NULL) AND id NOT IN (SELECT blob_id FROM offer_exports WHERE blob_id IS NOT NULL) AND id NOT IN (SELECT layout_blob_id FROM offer_template_versions) AND id NOT IN (SELECT draft_layout_blob_id FROM offer_templates WHERE draft_layout_blob_id IS NOT NULL);
   ```

**Not checked in the browser:** publishing version 2 and the AI using a newly saved prompt. Tests cover both, but I did not do them on the shared database.

**Leftovers and limits**

- Demo offer 5 still has a removed "Glossar" chapter, filled cells in the Mitwirkung table and one extra revision of the management summary.
- Word files exported before the cleaned layout still contain the old metadata.
- The sidebar shows "Angebote" twice, once under planning and once under administration. Admins cannot create new templates yet; they edit the seeded one.

# AGENTS.md

## 1) Golden Rules

1. **Think → Memory → Tools → Code → Memory.** Use code-reasoning; search Memory and claude-context first; minimal diff; write learnings back.
2. **Tests are truth.** Failures → fix code first. Change tests only if clearly wrong spec.
3. **Minimal diff.** Add tests before code. Keep simple.
4. **Consistency > cleverness.** Follow SOPs and stack idioms.
5. **Memory multiplies.** Persist decisions, patterns, error signatures, proven fixes.
6. **Files ≤ 1000 lines.** Exceed → refactor (see §5).
7. No extensive docs/summaries/comments unless requested.
8. No `--autogenerate` for Alembic migrations; write manually.
9. No `cat` to create files; use tools.
10. Log default: `logger.debug`. Important events: `logger.info`. Issues only: `logger.warning/error`. **No `print`.**
11. **Load `alloq-implementation` before any implementation task** (feature, fix, refactor, migration, tests); it maps Alloq's layers, guards and test recipes.

> Prefer *local* changes over cross-module refactors.

---

## 2) Task Bootstrap Pattern

```markdown
<!-- plan:start
goal: <one line clear goal>
constraints:
- Python 3.14; Reflex UI; FastAPI; SQLAlchemy 2.0; Alembic; Pydantic; appkit_mantine;
- logging: no f-strings in logger calls
- files ≤ 1000 lines; apply design patterns where appropriate
- minimal diff; add/adjust tests first
definition_of_done:
- tests pass; coverage ≥ 80% (non-Reflex classes & Reflex states); lint/type checks clean; memory updated
steps:
1) Search Memory for "<keywords>"
2) Draft/adjust failing test to capture expected behavior
3) Implement minimal code change
4) Run task test; iterate until green
5) Update Memory: decisions, patterns, error→fix
plan:end -->
```

---

## 3) Tooling Decision Matrix

| Situation | Primary | Secondary | Store to Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API/pattern uncertainty | **Context7** | — | Canonical snippet + link; edge cases |
| Ecosystem bug/issue | **DuckDuckGo** | Context7 | Minimal repro; versions; workaround |
| Repeated test failure | **Memory (search)** | Context7 | Error signature → fix; root cause |
| New feature scaffold | **Context7** | — | How‑to snippet; checklist |
| House style/tooling | **This file** | Context7 | Checklist results |

Prefer official docs; widen via web search for cross-version issues.

---

## 4) SOP — Development Workflow

**Task Runner:** `task` (via `Taskfile.dist.yml`), not `make`.

### Prepare

1. Memory first — search prior solutions.
2. Reasoning plan — Task Bootstrap Pattern.
3. `task sync` (uv, Python 3.14).
4. `task test` — snapshot current failures.

### Triage Failures

- Read first failing assertion; map to spec.
- Tests match spec → fix code. Diverge → document; adjust spec/tests (after approval).
- Add/adjust unit tests to codify expected behavior.

### Implement (Minimal Diff)

- Tests-first for new behavior. Approved stacks only. Apply design patterns (see §5).
- **No `print`.** Use `logging` module.
- **No f-strings in logger calls:**

  ```python
  import logging

  log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  log.info("Loaded items: %d", count)  # ✅
  # log.info(f"Loaded items: {count}") # ❌
  ```

- After every code change, run `task lint` — not just at PR time.

### Quality Gates

- `task lint`, `task format`, `task typecheck`.
- `task test` — coverage ≥ **80%** non-Reflex classes & Reflex states.

### Learn → write to **Memory**

### Dependencies

- add dependencies always be using `uv add <library name>`

---

## 5) Python Code & Testing

Full rules in **python-coding** skill. Key:

- Python 3.14; uv; line length **88**.
- No f-strings in logger calls.
- Files **≤ 1000 lines**.
- Test coverage ≥ 80%.
- Type annotations on **all** functions/methods.

---

## 6) Security & Config

- No credentials in code/history; `.env` local, Key Vault prod.
- Non-secret YAML; env `__` override pattern.
- Parameterized logs; no sensitive values.
- `SecretStr` → `.get_secret_value()`.
- Update vulnerable deps; document CVE-driven updates in commits & Memory.

---

## 7) Search SOPs

- **Context7 first** for framework truths; cite in Memory.
- **DuckDuckGo** for cross-version issues; prefer official docs.
- Store only final answer: minimal snippet + rationale + version pins + link.

---

## 8) Task Checklist / Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests added/updated; all green
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 80%
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck` pass
- [ ] No file > 1000 lines
- [ ] Clean architecture, no code smells, used python-clean-code principles
- [ ] Migrations reviewed & documented
- [ ] Documentation & README.md updated
- [ ] Memory updated (decisions, patterns, error→fix, learnings)

---

## 9) Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-implementation` | **Load first for every code change.** Alloq layers, handler authorization, test recipes, definition of done |
| `python-coding` | Python 3.14 style, logging, type annotations, design patterns, testing |
| `python-clean-code` | Enforce Clean Code Developer (CCD) architecture and software quality principles |
| `code-cleanup` | Refactor and simplify Python files modified in the current session if they get complex/big |
| `boost` | Use when the user wants to refine, sharpen, or expand a rough idea into a detailed implementation prompt |
| `reflex-state-and-architecture` | State design, event handlers, background tasks, form validation, page factory, service registry, repo pattern, DB models, architecture |
| `reflex-testing-state` | Pytest unit tests for Reflex State — event handlers, computed vars, substates |
| `reflex-docs` | Reflex.dev framework documentation |
| `frontend-design` | Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces |
| `appkit-mantine-reference` | Full API for appkit_mantine components — inputs, layout, overlays, charts, data display, navigation |
| `appkit-commons` | app configuration, service registry, DB repository pattern, DB entities, DB custom column types, scheduler |

# Entire repository agent guide — Brain

Use Brain for task context and retained knowledge. Begin substantive tasks needing
orientation with:

    entire brain brief "<task>" --json

Run it before deciding the task does not need it: what the brief adds is the part
you do not already know about.

Questions about why something is the way it is, what was decided, or what was
tried before are answered by durable memories. Retrieve them directly; the brief's
memories section is a sample, not the search:

# Refined prompt: Offer chapters as a document editor, templates and prompts in one "Angebote" admin menu — multiphase plan

> Load `alloq-implementation` first in **every** phase, then the skills listed under "Load first". Follow the test-first workflow and the definition of done of `alloq-implementation`. One phase = one reviewable commit. Do not start a phase before the previous one is green. Builds on `spec/plans/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (the workshop as it exists today).

### UI design (binding)

The Kapitel tab follows the board **"A + C · 2 Kapitel im Dokument: Kapiteltypen"** (`project/Kapitel.dc.html`) on the prototype canvas <https://claude.ai/artifact/SqvwnLbKttsfEL7XwnTcYX>. Read it before Phase 4 (Artifact tool, action `read`, `path` = `project/Kapitel.dc.html`) and match its layout, texts and states. Build with `mn.*`, Alloq shell parts and `alloq_commons/theme.py` tokens. Where this plan and the board differ, this plan wins (floating module toolbar, drag and drop, no story scope). Note every other deviation in the commit message.

## Context
The "Kapitel" tab of the offer workshop is a three-column list/editor/inspector today. Each
chapter is edited on its own, the outline is fixed by `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, and
chapter prompts are hard-wired. The prototype (screenshot "KI-gestützte Bearbeitung von
Kundenanfragen") shows the target: one continuous document that feels like a word processor,
an outline that the team can extend and reorder, and a context panel per chapter type.
Admins must be able to build templates from reusable chapter blocks and maintain the AI
prompts without a code change.

The work is large. Implement it in the phases below, one phase per commit, each phase green
on `task lint`, `task typecheck` and `task test` before the next starts.

---

## Task
1. Rebuild the Kapitel tab as a document view like the prototype: outline left, all
   chapters as stacked blocks in the middle, a chapter panel right. Only the selected
   chapter is editable and shows its own toolbar.
2. Let users add chapters (from the library or blank), remove optional ones, and reorder
   them by drag and drop. Required chapters cannot be removed. The fixed legal frame of the
   Word layout stays pinned at start and end.
3. Move templates, reusable chapter blocks, rule checks, the Word layout and all AI prompts
   from code files into the database, edited in one new admin menu "Angebote".

## Load first
`alloq-implementation` (mandatory), then `reflex-state-and-architecture`,
`appkit-mantine-reference`, `appkit-commons`, `reflex-testing-state`, `german-ui-copy`.

## Existing code to build on (all under `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/`)
| Area | Files | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Template loader | `export/template_package.py` | `load_template(key)` (cached) builds `TemplatePackage` from YAML + `layout.docx`; `ChapterDef`, `CHAPTER_ANCHOR`, `check_layout()` |
| Template call sites | `services/chapters.py`, `services/findings.py`, `services/workspace.py`, `services/export_snapshot.py`, `jobs/draft_chapters.py`, `jobs/export_docx.py` | All call `load_template(workspace.template_key)` |
| Template data | `templates/quo_v1/chapters.yaml`, `rules.yaml`, `layout.docx` | Layout holds the legal frame (Rechtlicher Hinweis, Inhaltsverzeichnis before `[[KAPITEL]]`; Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist, Sonstiges, Anlagen, Unterschriften after) |
| Content model | `content/schema.py`, `content/editor_io.py`, `content/text.py` | Types `prose`, `table`, `stories`, `calc`; HTML ⇄ block tree |
| Chapters service | `services/chapters.py` | Revisions, conflict check (A08), proposals, protection, `default_content()`, `mark_dependent_review()` |
| Chapter state / UI | `states/chapter_state.py`, `components/chapters_tab.py`, `components/review_panel.py` | Autosave with debounce, AI help, history, findings |
| Entities | `entities.py` | `WorkspaceEntity.template_key/template_version`, `ChapterEntity` (unique `offer_id, chapter_key`), `ChapterRevisionEntity`, `ProposalEntity`, `FindingEntity`, `SnapshotEntity`, `BlobEntity` |
| Blob storage | `storage.py`, `BlobEntity` | Reuse for uploaded layout files |
| Prompts | `ai/agents.py` (`load_prompt`, `*_PROMPT` names, `*_prompt_version` attrs), `ai/prompts/*.md`, `ai/render.py`, `ai/port.py`, `ai/demo.py` | `GenerationRunEntity` records the prompt version |
| Export | `export/docx_renderer.py`, `export/chapter_renderers.py` | Uses `chapter.title/level` from the snapshot |
| Admin pages | `app/pages/industries.py` (pattern: `app_page(..., admin_only=True)`, `window_toolbar`, `requires_admin`), `app/components/sidebar.py` (`ADMIN` nav list) | |
| Editor | `mn.rich_text_editor` (`appkit_mantine/tiptap.py`) has `show_toolbar`, `sticky`, `sticky_offset`, `editable`, `control_groups` | |
| Theme/CSS | `alloq_commons/theme.py`, `assets/css/aq-workshop.css` | |

Repo rules that apply (from memory and CLAUDE.md):
- Offers are edited by `offer_editor` only (`requires_offer_editor`), admins do not edit offers.
  The admin menu needs the admin switch (`requires_admin` on the page and on every handler).
- Big state logic goes into mixins, not substates. Keep DB handlers in the module tests patch.
- Static layout CSS goes in `assets/css/aq-*.css`. Page popovers use `theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX`.
- Hand-written Alembic revisions in `alembic/versions/` (date-prefixed names). Never run
  `alembic upgrade`; hand the command to the user. Run the `migration-reviewer` agent.
- Sort German names in Python, not in SQL. Files ≤ 1000 lines. No f-strings in logger calls.
- German UI text, Sie-form, as in the existing tab.

---

## Decisions (agreed with the user)
- **Frame:** the legal blocks from the Word layout stay pinned at start and end and cannot
  be moved or removed. Required content chapters can be moved but not removed. Optional and
  added chapters can be moved and removed.
- **"+ Kapitel"** offers library blocks (with default content, rules and prompt) and a blank
  chapter of a chosen type (Text, Tabelle, User Stories, Werte).
- **Prompts:** global system prompts (chapter, map, map additions, briefing, review) are
  editable and versioned in admin. Each library block adds its own instructions on top
  (Leitfrage, Regeln, extra prompt text).
- **Admin scope now:** templates, chapter blocks, prompts, Word layout upload, rule checks.
  Branchen stays on its own page.
- **Template changes never alter existing offers** (spec 6.1). A template is edited as a
  draft and published as an immutable version. A workspace binds `template_key` +
  `template_version`. On creation the offer copies the outline and chapter settings into its
  own chapters.

---

## Phase 1: Data model and migration
New entities in a new module `workshop/template_entities.py` (keeps `entities.py` under the
line limit):
- `ChapterBlockEntity` (`offer_chapter_blocks`): `key` (unique slug), `title`,
  `chapter_type`, `level` (1 or 2), `default_content` (JSON, validated by `parse_content`),
  `guiding_question`, `content_rules` (JSON list), `prompt_text`, `required_info` (JSON list),
  `checks` (JSON list, values limited to the check names known in `services/checks.py`),
  `active`.
- `OfferTemplateEntity` (`offer_templates`): `key` (unique), `name`, `description`, `active`,
  `draft_layout_blob_id`, `frame_before` / `frame_after` (JSON lists of headings).
- `OfferTemplateChapterEntity` (`offer_template_chapters`): `template_id`, `block_id`,
  `position`, `required`, optional `title` and `level` overrides. Draft outline only.
- `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` (`offer_template_versions`): `template_id`, `number`,
  `payload` (JSON: full outline with resolved block settings, frame lists), `layout_blob_id`,
  `published_by`, `created`. Immutable.
- `PromptEntity` (`offer_prompts`): `name` (chapter, map, map_additions, briefing, review),
  `version` (int), `text`, `active`, `author`. Unique (`name`, `version`); one active per name.

Changes to `ChapterEntity`: add `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`, `required`,
`block_key` (nullable, origin library block), `settings` (JSON snapshot: guiding question,
rules, prompt text, required_info, checks), `removed_at` (soft delete, so revisions, findings
and restore keep working). New chapters added in an offer get key `custom_<8 hex>`.

Migration (one hand-written revision):
1. Create the tables above.
2. Add the new `offer_chapters` columns (nullable first).
3. Seed: one `ChapterBlockEntity` per entry of `quo_v1/chapters.yaml` (rules from
   `rules.yaml`), template `quo_v1` with its draft outline and published version `1`
   (`payload` from the YAML, layout bytes stored as a blob, `frame_before`/`frame_after`
   read from the layout headings), and the five prompts from `ai/prompts/*.md` as version 1.
   Version string mapping: existing workspaces keep `template_version = "quo_v1.0"`; map
   that to version 1.
4. Backfill existing `offer_chapters` rows: `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`,
   `required`, `block_key`, `settings` from the seeded quo_v1 payload. Then set NOT NULL.
Seed data lives in the migration as literals (no import of app code). After the migration,
delete `templates/quo_v1/*.yaml` and `ai/prompts/*.md`. Keep `layout.docx` only as a test
fixture under `tests/fixtures/` if tests need it.

## Phase 2: DB-backed template and prompt access
- Replace `load_template` with a `TemplateService` (`services/templates.py`) that loads a
  published `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` by (`key`, `version`) into the existing
  `TemplatePackage` shape. `layout_bytes` comes from the blob instead of a file path. Keep a
  small in-process cache keyed by (`key`, `version`); versions are immutable so no
  invalidation is needed.
- Per-offer code must use the offer's own chapters, not the template: `mark_dependent_review`,
  `services/findings.py` (rules per chapter now come from `ChapterEntity.settings`),
  `jobs/draft_chapters.py` (guiding question, rules and prompt text from `settings`),
  `services/export_snapshot.py` (order by `position`, skip `removed_at`, title/level from the
  chapter). Only `services/workspace.py` (new offer) and `jobs/export_docx.py` (layout and
  frame) still need the template version.
- `services/workspace.py`: on open, pick the latest published version of the default (or
  chosen) template and copy its outline into `offer_chapters` with `default_content` as
  revision 1.
- `ai/agents.py`: `load_prompt(name)` reads the active `PromptEntity`; the agent's
  `*_prompt_version` attributes become `"<name>@<version>"` so `GenerationRunEntity` keeps
  recording which prompt text ran. The chapter request (`ai/port.py`, `ai/render.py`) gets the
  chapter's `prompt_text` as an extra tagged section after Leitfrage and Regeln. `ai/demo.py`
  keeps working without DB prompts.

## Phase 3: Outline operations in the chapters service
Add to `services/chapters.py` (or a new `services/outline.py` if the file would pass 1000
lines; keep the DB calls where tests patch them):
- `add_chapter(offer_id, after_key, block_key | chapter_type, title)`: inserts at the given
  position, revision 1 from block default content or the empty default of the type.
- `remove_chapter(offer_id, key)`: refuses required chapters ("Pflichtkapitel können nicht
  entfernt werden."), sets `removed_at`. A removed chapter can be restored from a small
  "Entfernte Kapitel" list.
- `move_chapter(offer_id, key, new_index)`: renumbers positions in one transaction; the frame
  is not part of the list, so it can never be moved.
- `rename_chapter(offer_id, key, title)` and `set_level(offer_id, key, level)`.

## Decisions (agreed with the user)
- **Frame:** the legal blocks from the Word layout stay pinned at start and end and cannot
  be moved or removed. Required content chapters can be moved but not removed. Optional and
  added chapters can be moved and removed.
- **"+ Kapitel"** offers library blocks (with default content, rules and prompt) and a blank
  chapter of a chosen type (Text, Tabelle, User Stories, Werte).
- **Prompts:** global system prompts (chapter, map, map additions, briefing, review) are
  editable and versioned in admin. Each library block adds its own instructions on top
  (Leitfrage, Regeln, extra prompt text).
- **Admin scope now:** templates, chapter blocks, prompts, Word layout upload, rule checks.
  Branchen stays on its own page.
- **Template changes never alter existing offers** (spec 6.1). A template is edited as a
  draft and published as an immutable version. A workspace binds `template_key` +
  `template_version`. On creation the offer copies the outline and chapter settings into its
  own chapters.

## Phase 1: Data model and migration
New entities in a new module `workshop/template_entities.py` (keeps `entities.py` under the
line limit):
- `ChapterBlockEntity` (`offer_chapter_blocks`): `key` (unique slug), `title`,
  `chapter_type`, `level` (1 or 2), `default_content` (JSON, validated by `parse_content`),
  `guiding_question`, `content_rules` (JSON list), `prompt_text`, `required_info` (JSON list),
  `checks` (JSON list, values limited to the check names known in `services/checks.py`),
  `active`.
- `OfferTemplateEntity` (`offer_templates`): `key` (unique), `name`, `description`, `active`,
  `draft_layout_blob_id`, `frame_before` / `frame_after` (JSON lists of headings).
- `OfferTemplateChapterEntity` (`offer_template_chapters`): `template_id`, `block_id`,
  `position`, `required`, optional `title` and `level` overrides. Draft outline only.
- `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` (`offer_template_versions`): `template_id`, `number`,
  `payload` (JSON: full outline with resolved block settings, frame lists), `layout_blob_id`,
  `published_by`, `created`. Immutable.
- `PromptEntity` (`offer_prompts`): `name` (chapter, map, map_additions, briefing, review),
  `version` (int), `text`, `active`, `author`. Unique (`name`, `version`); one active per name.

Changes to `ChapterEntity`: add `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`, `required`,
`block_key` (nullable, origin library block), `settings` (JSON snapshot: guiding question,
rules, prompt text, required_info, checks), `removed_at` (soft delete, so revisions, findings
and restore keep working). New chapters added in an offer get key `custom_<8 hex>`.

Migration (one hand-written revision):
1. Create the tables above.
2. Add the new `offer_chapters` columns (nullable first).
3. Seed: one `ChapterBlockEntity` per entry of `quo_v1/chapters.yaml` (rules from
   `rules.yaml`), template `quo_v1` with its draft outline and published version `1`
   (`payload` from the YAML, layout bytes stored as a blob, `frame_before`/`frame_after`
   read from the layout headings), and the five prompts from `ai/prompts/*.md` as version 1.
   Version string mapping: existing workspaces keep `template_version = "quo_v1.0"`; map
   that to version 1.
4. Backfill existing `offer_chapters` rows: `position`, `title`, `chapter_type`, `level`,
   `required`, `block_key`, `settings` from the seeded quo_v1 payload. Then set NOT NULL.
Seed data lives in the migration as literals (no import of app code). After the migration,
delete `templates/quo_v1/*.yaml` and `ai/prompts/*.md`. Keep `layout.docx` only as a test
fixture under `tests/fixtures/` if tests need it.

  published `OfferTemplateVersionEntity` by (`key`, `version`) into the existing
  `TemplatePackage` shape. `layout_bytes` comes from the blob instead of a file path. Keep a
  small in-process cache keyed by (`key`, `version`); versions are immutable so no
  invalidation is needed.
- Per-offer code must use the offer's own chapters, not the template: `mark_dependent_review`,
  `services/findings.py` (rules per chapter now come from `ChapterEntity.settings`),
  `jobs/draft_chapters.py` (guiding question, rules and prompt text from `settings`),
  `services/export_snapshot.py` (order by `position`, skip `removed_at`, title/level from the
  chapter). Only `services/workspace.py` (new offer) and `jobs/export_docx.py` (layout and
  frame) still need the template version.
- `services/workspace.py`: on open, pick the latest published version of the default (or
  chosen) template and copy its outline into `offer_chapters` with `default_content` as
  revision 1.
- `ai/agents.py`: `load_prompt(name)` reads the active `PromptEntity`; the agent's

## Phase 3: Outline operations in the chapters service
Add to `services/chapters.py` (or a new `services/outline.py` if the file would pass 1000
lines; keep the DB calls where tests patch them):

  entfernt werden."), sets `removed_at`. A removed chapter can be restored from a small
  "Entfernte Kapitel" list.
- `move_chapter(offer_id, key, new_index)`: renumbers positions in one transaction; the frame
  is not part of the list, so it can never be moved.

from alloq_commons.models.department import Department
from appkit_commons.roles import Role

PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE = Role(
    id=1,
    name="project_manager",
    label="Projektmanager",
    description="Voller Zugriff auf Planung, Projekte und Team, ohne Administration",
)

EMPLOYEE_ROLE = Role(
    id=2,
    name="employee",
    label="Mitarbeiter",
    description="Lesezugriff auf Projekte und Ressourcenplanung",
)

OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE = Role(
    id=3,
    name="offer_editor",
    label="Angebote",
    description="Lesen und Bearbeiten der Angebote",
)

ALL_ROLES: list[Role] = [
    PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE,
    EMPLOYEE_ROLE,
    OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE,
]

DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP = "Abteilungen"


def department_role_name(department_id: int) -> str:
    """Permission role name of a department; keyed by id so renames keep it."""
    return f"department_{department_id}"


def department_roles(departments: list[Department]) -> list[Role]:
    """Permission roles offered in user management, one per department."""
    return [

            label=d.label,
            description=f"Mitglied der Abteilung {d.name}",
            group=DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP,

    ]

async def _workspace(self, session: AsyncSession) -> WorkspaceEntity:
        workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, self._offer_id)
        if workspace is None:
            raise ChapterError(NOT_FOUND)
        await session.refresh(workspace, with_for_update=True)
        await ensure_open(session, self._offer_id)
        return workspace

    async def _chapter(self, session: AsyncSession, key: str) -> ChapterEntity:
        await self._workspace(session)
        chapter = await find_chapter(session, self._offer_id, key, lock=True)
        return ensure_editable(chapter)

    async def _used_blocks(self, session: AsyncSession) -> set[str]:
        """Blocks of the offer, removed chapters too: those come back by restore."""
        keys = await session.scalars(
            select(ChapterEntity.block_key).where(
                ChapterEntity.offer_id == self._offer_id,
                ChapterEntity.block_key.is_not(None),
            )
        )
        return {key for key in keys.all() if key}

    async def library(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Active blocks the offer does not use yet, by title."""
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            used = await self._used_blocks(session)
            blocks = (
                await session.scalars(
                    select(ChapterBlockEntity).where(ChapterBlockEntity.active)
                )
            ).all()
        return [
            {
                "key": block.key,
                "title": block.title,
                "type": block.chapter_type,
                "description": block.guiding_question,
            }
            for block in sorted(blocks, key=lambda b: german_sort_key(b.title))
            if block.key not in used
        ]

    async def removed(self) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
        """Removed chapters, last removed first."""
    async def add_chapter(
        self,
        after_key: str | None,
        *,
        block_key: str | None = None,
        chapter_type: str = "",
        title: str = "",
    ) -> str:
        """Insert a library block, or else a blank chapter of ``chapter_type``.

        It goes after ``after_key``, or last without one; returns the new key.
        """
        # An older offer gets its template chapters before anything is added.
        await ChapterService(self._sessions, self._offer_id, self._user).open()
        async with self._sessions() as session:
            workspace = await self._workspace(session)
            chapters = await live_chapters(session, self._offer_id)
            if len(chapters) >= MAX_CHAPTERS:
                raise ChapterError(TOO_MANY)
            keys = [c.chapter_key for c in chapters]
            if after_key is not None and after_key not in keys:
                raise ChapterError(NOT_FOUND)
            index = len(chapters) if after_key is None else keys.index(after_key) + 1
            key = f"{NEW_KEY_PREFIX}{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
            # A blank chapter joins the level of the chapter it follows.
            level = chapters[index - 1].level if index else 1

def render_chapter(request: ChapterRequest, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """The chapter task with map and briefing as delimited data."""
    parts = [
        f'<kapitel titel="{_attr(request.title)}">',
        f"Leitfrage: {_tags(request.guiding_question)}",
        *(f"Regel: {_tags(rule)}" for rule in request.rules),
        *(f"Pflichtangabe: {_tags(info)}" for info in request.required_info),
        *(
            [f"{TABLE_TASK} {' | '.join(map(_tags, request.columns))}"]
            if request.columns
            else []
        ),
        "</kapitel>",
    ]
    if request.prompt_text.strip():
        parts += [
            "<kapitelanweisung>",
            _tags(request.prompt_text),
            "</kapitelanweisung>",
        ]
    if request.current_lines:
        lines = [_tags(line) for line in request.current_lines]
        parts += ["<aktueller_text>", *lines, "</aktueller_text>"]
    if request.instruction:
        parts += ["<anweisung>", _tags(request.instruction), "</anweisung>"]

        ),

    ]

            "<kapitelanweisung>",

The plan is fully implemented. The review found two small gaps, and I fixed both (commit a6bca6d). Lint, type check and all 2389 tests pass, with 92.6 % coverage. Nothing is pushed yet.

## Gaps found and fixed

- **Missing log lines:** the plan says every admin write logs one info line. Adding, removing, moving and changing entries of a template draft did not log anything. They now log ids only, never titles, and a test checks this.
- **Type name:** the "+ Kapitel" dialog and the block editor offered the stories type as "Stories". The plan calls it "User Stories", so they now use that name. The small badge in the outline still says "Stories".

## Phase by phase

| Phase | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Data model and migration | Complete: five new tables, new chapter columns, seed data, backfill, the `custom_<hex>` key for added chapters. The YAML and prompt files are deleted. |
| 2 Templates and prompts from the database | Complete: offers use their own chapters for checks, AI drafts and the export. Prompts are recorded as `name@version`. Each chapter's extra prompt text reaches the AI. |
| 3 Outline operations | Complete: add (after the selected chapter), remove, restore, move, rename, set the level, and numbering. Protected chapters and archived offers are locked. A chapter moved to the top becomes level 1. |
| 4 Document view | Complete: the modules, both mixins, the floating toolbar for each chapter type, all panel parts, the "+ Kapitel" dialog and drag and drop with the keyboard. |
| 5 Admin menu | Complete, with three changes from the plan. All three are noted in the commit message. |
| 6 Docs | Complete, and the docs check passed. |

The three changes in Phase 5:
- The template list only shows when there is more than one template. Admins cannot create a new template yet.
- Only text blocks use the real chapter editor for their start content. Table, stories and calc blocks use simple fields.
- The sidebar shows "Angebote" twice, once under planning and once under administration.

## Success criteria from the plan

- Tests cover these:
  - The Word export follows a moved, removed and added chapter.
  - Publishing creates version 2, new offers use it and existing offers keep version 1.
  - A saved prompt becomes `chapter@2`.
- I did not do these in the browser on the shared database:
  - publishing version 2 and then creating a new offer;
  - an AI draft after a prompt change.
- You still need to run the migration yourself:

```bash
uv run alembic upgrade head
```

## The workshop role

The role is available.

- **Where it is defined:** `offer_editor` (shown as "Angebote", "Lesen und Bearbeiten der Angebote") is in [roles.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/roles.py) and is part of `ALL_ROLES`.
- **How to assign it:** the user admin page `/admin/users` offers it when it loads (`load_user_roles`). Roles are defined in code, so no migration is needed.
- **Who gets in:** the workshop page and every workshop handler check this role (`requires_offer_editor`). Being an admin is not enough (`has_role` ignores the admin switch).
- **What this means:** an admin can manage templates, blocks and prompts in `/admin/offers`. An admin can only open the workshop after also getting the role "Angebote" in the user admin page.

def app_page(
    route: str,
    title: str,
    sidebar: rx.Component,
    *,
    toolbar: rx.Component | None = None,
    scope: rx.Component | None = None,
    padded: bool = True,
    admin_only: bool = False,
    on_load: EventType[()] | Sequence[Any] | None = None,
) -> Callable[[Callable[[], rx.Component]], rx.Component]:
    """Authenticated page in the app shell.

    Registers the route through appkit's ``authenticated_page`` (session
    monitor, admin gate, loading state) with our window as template.
    """
    handlers = desktop_handlers(on_load)

    def template(content: rx.Component) -> rx.Component:
        window = app_layout(sidebar, toolbar, content, scope=scope, padded=padded)
        return rx.fragment(splash(), window) if is_desktop() else window

    return authenticated_page(
        route=route,
        title=title,
        template=template,
        admin_only=admin_only,
        on_load=cast("Any", handlers),
    )
